title: Cinema Emotion Node editorial catalog
editorial_notice: Creative performance options, not diagnostic signs or validated intensity thresholds. Select compatible cues; preserve individual context and voice identity.

emotions.label: Fear
emotions.definition: A response to an identifiable perceived danger, organized around protecting what matters when safety is uncertain. Its outward form may be escape, skilled action, concealment, appeal or immobility.
emotions.appraisal: Something here can harm me or someone I value; I must judge distance, options and the cost of moving.
emotions.objective: Locate a usable safety option and preserve the ability to choose it without surrendering the threatened person or object.
action_tendencies: Track the threat and available protection.
Escape or increase distance when possible.
Shield someone, seek assistance or prepare a defense.
Become still to avoid detection or gather information.
distinctions: Anxiety monitors uncertain future possibilities; fear has a more identifiable present target.
Panic adds felt loss of organized coping; fear can support precise, practiced action.
Horror includes appalled recognition or rejection of what has occurred, beyond a direct safety calculation.

face.brows_forehead: Inner brows can lift while their centers draw together.
face.eyelids: Upper lids may uncover more eye; lower lids can brace.
face.gaze: Choose threat, exit or protected person as distinct targets; light governs pupils.
face.blink: A blink may be delayed during tracking, then released.
face.cheeks: Cheeks may hold against a contained mouth.
face.nose_nostrils: Nostrils may respond to comfortable breathing, without required flare.
face.lips_mouth: Lips part to prepare speech or narrow to conceal it.
face.jaw_chin: Jaw may set briefly, then release for a practical instruction.
face.head_neck: Chin retracts or head angles to preserve sightlines.
face.complexion: No required pallor; color depends on individual baseline and lighting.

voice.pitch_register: Register may lift under alarm or lower deliberately for concealment.
voice.pitch_range_contour: Contour can climb on uncertainty, then flatten for instructions.
voice.loudness: Choose audible warning or reduced volume according to detection risk.
voice.tempo_rhythm: A clipped start may alternate with slowed tactical phrases.
voice.stress: Place emphasis on location, person or immediate safety verb.
voice.articulation: Precise consonants can communicate control; hurried endings may shorten.
voice.resonance: Forward, compact placement can keep a quiet instruction legible.
voice.texture: Light tremor or dry edges are optional, never forced constriction.
voice.breath_phrasing: Use comfortable short phrases and natural replenishing breaths.
voice.pauses: Pause to listen or evaluate rather than decorate every word.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A small intake, startled syllable or quiet exhale may precede speech.

body.head_neck: Head can lead attention while neck limits unnecessary motion.
body.shoulders: Shoulders may gather protectively or remain trained and low.
body.chest_torso: Torso angles toward cover while keeping the threat observable.
body.arms_elbows: Elbows stay available for shielding or balance.
body.hands_fingers: Fingers release an object slowly or secure one useful grip.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight prepares an exit without requiring an actual step.
body.legs_feet: Feet choose support and direction appropriate to mobility.
body.gait: Movement may be measured, sudden or entirely withheld.
body.proxemics: Distance is negotiated among threat, cover and vulnerable others.
body.touch_props: Props become cover, communication tools or something to protect.
body.stillness: Stillness may be an active attempt not to be detected.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: A possible danger interrupts ordinary attention without yet taking over the scene.
levels.face: Let the brows gather for one observation, with lids opening just enough to inspect. Shift gaze from the speaker to the suspicious detail, then return. Keep the mouth usable; let a small jaw pause interrupt an otherwise ordinary expression.
levels.voice: Begin near the character’s normal register with a brief upward question contour. Keep tone clear and volume conversational; shorten one phrase, then leave a listening pause. A natural replenishing breath carries the next words, with one safety-relevant word receiving more precise stress.
levels.body: Interrupt a casual hand action before changing overall posture. Let the head orient first, torso following only enough to improve the view. Reposition weight on the existing support and leave feet or mobility aid ready without initiating escape.
levels.timing: The cue earns one extra beat of attention before conversation resumes with divided focus.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the social expression intact; reveal the concern only through a delayed glance back.
levels.recovery: A benign explanation allows the hand action and ordinary conversational rhythm to finish.
levels.playable_direction: Check whether that small change matters while keeping the other person at ease.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: The danger seems plausible enough to justify a precaution and a second look.
levels.face: Hold the gaze on the target longer; bring the brow centers closer and brace the lower lids. Lips part for a practical question, then close while listening. Let the chin pull back a fraction when the distance feels insufficient.
levels.voice: Use a slightly elevated register for checking, dropping toward baseline when proposing a precaution. Tone stays usable with a faint dry edge; volume remains moderate. Place shorter clauses around listening pauses and let comfortable breaths arrive between questions rather than building a breathless stream.
levels.body: Angle the chest toward a safer route and bring one elbow nearer the body. Set down an unnecessary prop deliberately. Shift the pelvis toward the better support, with feet, chair or assistive device oriented for a possible change of position.
levels.timing: Alternate information gathering with a small concrete adjustment after each answer.
levels.restrained_alternative: Offer an ordinary practical reason for repositioning; allow the eyes to keep monitoring.
levels.recovery: Specific reassurance reduces checking before the body fully returns to its former orientation.
levels.playable_direction: Make a small safety improvement without announcing that you are frightened.

levels.label: Clear
levels.felt_state: The threat is recognizable; attention organizes around protecting self or another person.
levels.face: Raise and knit the inner brows while maintaining a direct, selective gaze. Open the lips for a warning; let the jaw stabilize its delivery. Look once toward the person needing protection, then return to the danger instead of scanning indiscriminately.
levels.voice: Choose a register slightly above baseline with a decisive falling contour on the instruction. The tone is alert and clear, with moderate firm loudness. Accelerate the warning, pause to confirm it landed, and use an easy breath to deliver the next short, articulated clause.
levels.body: Move one arm into a shielding or guiding position while the torso takes a useful angle. Establish a stable base and create room for a retreat if the scene permits. Hands carry out a task instead of fluttering without purpose.
levels.timing: The first clear recognition produces a warning, followed immediately by checking its effect.
levels.restrained_alternative: Deliver the same instruction quietly with exact eye contact and minimal visible movement.
levels.recovery: Once protected, permit a delayed exhale and inspect whether the other person is actually safe.
levels.playable_direction: Get the vulnerable person to understand what they must do next.

levels.label: Strong
levels.felt_state: The danger is close enough that every choice carries a noticeable cost.
levels.face: Fix gaze on the threat through a longer unbroken look; brows stay drawn and lids alert. The mouth may stretch briefly before narrowing around words. Give the exit one economical glance and let the chin tuck as the head turns back.
levels.voice: Let the initial register rise, then deliberately narrow the contour to make directions intelligible. Tone can acquire a thin or lightly uneven edge; use firm rather than automatically loud volume. Speech comes in urgent units separated by listening and comfortable breaths, with no decorative hesitation.
levels.body: Gather the torso over reliable support and keep elbows close enough to protect the center. A hand can guide another person or brace a door. Let the lower body commit to a chosen direction while upper-body attention still tracks the threat.
levels.timing: Compress decisions; make each still interval feel like active listening for the next opening.
levels.restrained_alternative: Use trained precision: stable posture, low volume, and only the eyes revealing the stakes.
levels.recovery: Safety first restores task completion; shaking or emotional release, if chosen, can arrive afterward.
levels.playable_direction: Choose the least dangerous next action and commit before the opening closes.

levels.label: Intense
levels.felt_state: The threat dominates awareness, yet a narrow workable action still exists.
levels.face: Allow a marked widening around the eyes or a hard protective squint, choosing according to the actual hazard. Brows pull centrally; the mouth remains open only until words are needed. Anchor gaze on one actionable point, with a brief tremor at the lips optional.
levels.voice: Use a register that jumps on the first warning and settles into a narrow urgent band. Tone may be airy at entry, then clearer on the essential noun. Loudness follows distance; keep phrases short, pacing immediate, and take easy intervening breaths instead of forcing sustained shouting.
levels.body: Bring body mass behind the chosen protective task: brace, guide, withdraw or hold position. Remove competing gestures. Feet and pelvis secure balance; fingers may grip one useful surface and release when a new action requires it.
levels.timing: Action and perception alternate in sharp beats; unrelated speech barely earns a response.
levels.restrained_alternative: Let extreme fear appear as exact, quiet compliance while a fixed gaze checks the escape opportunity.
levels.recovery: After immediate danger passes, orientation broadens gradually to sounds, people and ordinary objects.
levels.playable_direction: Do the one thing that can still change the outcome.

levels.label: Consuming
levels.felt_state: Safety feels almost unavailable; protecting a final option absorbs the whole scene.
levels.face: Hold the face between a warning that cannot yet be given and the need to watch. Lids stay intensely engaged, brows high or tightly gathered. Let the lips form a name without sound, then fix gaze on the smallest sign of opportunity.
levels.voice: The register can hover high on a fragment or settle unusually low in concealment. Keep texture fragile but unforced; loudness may be only enough for one listener. Slow at the crucial word, pause to listen, and let each comfortable breath support a separate essential message.
levels.body: Choose sustained guarded stillness or a focused protective effort. Keep torso and pelvis organized around cover, contact or balance. One hand may maintain reassurance on another person while the rest of the body withholds movement that could expose them.
levels.timing: Expand the waiting beat subjectively while preserving sudden readiness at a meaningful cue.
levels.restrained_alternative: A nearly ordinary face can coexist with rigidly selective attention and one carefully timed response.
levels.recovery: Even after reassurance, test safety through a concrete observation before allowing touch or movement.
levels.playable_direction: Preserve this final chance without giving away your intention.

levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: Danger occupies almost all available attention; action may reduce to a single protective choice.
levels.face: Choose a fixed, scarcely blinking stare or closed lids against a seen impact; do not combine them. Brows and mouth may lock into an unfinished expression. A small gaze return toward the endangered person carries more meaning than continuously enlarged facial movement.
levels.voice: Speech may reduce to one clear word in a narrow register, repeated only when action requires it. Tone can be quiet, thin or unexpectedly steady; volume need not peak. Leave long perception-driven gaps, use comfortable breaths, and let any fuller sentence require an explicit return of attention.
levels.body: Let the entire posture serve one act: remain concealed, shield, reach for help or maintain support. Eliminate unrelated motion. An inhibited body can be fully engaged; if movement occurs, align head, torso and base before changing location safely.
levels.timing: Hold the decisive beat until a real environmental change permits a new response.
levels.restrained_alternative: Play complete outward composure with a narrowed field of attention and delayed response to nonessential speech.
levels.recovery: Recover through one verified safety cue, then another; social expression may return later than movement.
levels.playable_direction: Keep one person alive in your attention and let everything else fall away.

variants.label: Concealed escape
variants.context: The character must appear cooperative while assessing a way out.
variants.objective: Find an exit without revealing that leaving is being considered.
variants.face_modifier: Keep the social mouth composed while gaze checks practical landmarks.
variants.voice_modifier: Favor low audibility and intact everyday syntax until concealment is no longer useful.
variants.body_modifier: Orient support or seating subtly; choose one prop action that disguises preparation.
variants.timing_modifier: Let escape assessments occur during the other person’s speech.

seven_levels.modifier: Notice an exit while completing the ordinary greeting; let the eyes return before the host can follow their glance.
Ask an innocent question that reveals who controls the door, allowing a small listening pause after the answer.
Place a carried object where it can be retrieved quickly, keeping the conversational face available to the host.
Cover a clearer shift toward the exit with an everyday practical action, then wait to see whether it was noticed.
Make speech simpler while preserving politeness; privately commit to the first usable opening rather than checking every possibility.
Give one carefully timed agreeable response while the body waits in an exact position that permits departure.
Let the performance shrink to apparent compliance and one decisive assessment; a tiny environmental cue releases the prepared action.

variants.label: Protecting another person
variants.context: The perceived danger primarily threatens someone the character wants to keep safe.
variants.objective: Secure the other person’s attention and guide them toward protection.
variants.face_modifier: Route gaze between danger and the protected person; reassurance may soften the mouth without relaxing monitoring.
variants.voice_modifier: Address the protected person with clear, usable phrases and a contour they can follow.
variants.body_modifier: Use consensual guiding contact or an available equivalent; make distance protective rather than possessive.
variants.timing_modifier: Check comprehension before the next instruction.

seven_levels.modifier: Glance at the other person to confirm they noticed the questionable detail, then offer a small precaution without alarm.
Create a little more space around them and use their name once to gather attention before giving practical information.
Let the warning begin only after eye contact; guide their attention to the safe option rather than dramatizing the threat.
Repeat a single instruction more clearly when they hesitate, keeping your own body oriented between their position and danger.
Use a calmer tone toward them than toward the threat; every touch, if welcome, communicates the next action.
Keep checking that they remain with you; allow the voice to reveal strain only during the moment they cannot see your face.
Choose one final protective act and sustain it; a quiet name or exact instruction may carry the entire emotional peak.

temporal_arc.onset: A sensory detail or new information interrupts an existing action.
temporal_arc.escalation: Checking identifies stakes, distance and narrowing safety options.
temporal_arc.apex: A protective action or deliberate immobility becomes the dominant behavior.
temporal_arc.recovery: Verified safety permits attention to widen before social ease returns.
temporal_arc.carryover: Residual checking, tenderness, irritation or delayed trembling may remain without being obligatory.

transitions.trigger: The immediate danger is credibly removed.
transitions.bridge: Let gaze verify the safe condition before releasing the mouth and widening breath phrasing.

transitions.trigger: Available coping options feel lost and attention becomes difficult to organize.
transitions.bridge: A once coherent instruction fragments as gaze searches for an answer it cannot retain.

transitions.trigger: The character identifies a preventable agent of the danger.
transitions.bridge: Redirect the tracking gaze toward that person and replace protective questions with a boundary-setting demand.

prompt_example.spoken_text: I thought you would be here.
prompt_example.visual_direction: Pause the ordinary hand action, check the doorway, then hold the other person’s gaze while keeping a usable exit in peripheral attention.
prompt_example.delivery_direction: Use a contained, alert tone; stress “here” as the location that was supposed to mean safety, with a listening pause afterward.

cue_conflicts: A wide-eyed alert face and a protective squint are alternatives chosen for different hazards, not a mandatory combined mask.
Silent concealment and shouted warning depend on detection risk and recipient distance.
Stillness can be strategic fear; visible fleeing is not required for higher levels.
emotions.context_notes: Calibrate against this character’s habits, training, relationship and power to act. Culture affects permissible display and help seeking; use seated, assisted or nonlocomotor protective choices when appropriate. No selected cue proves fear, and a close-up need only activate visible regions.

emotions.label: Anxiety
emotions.definition: An apprehensive state sustained by possible adverse outcomes whose likelihood, timing or manageability remains unresolved. Attention repeatedly returns to what might happen even while ordinary activity continues.
emotions.appraisal: I cannot yet tell whether things will be safe or whether I will cope, so preparation and monitoring feel necessary.
emotions.objective: Obtain enough dependable information, preparation or support to tolerate the unresolved outcome.
action_tendencies: Maintain routine as a way of containing uncertainty.
distinctions: Fear typically has a more identifiable immediate threat; anxiety can persist without one.
Worry is the repeated thinking process that may accompany anxiety, not its complete felt state.
Anticipation can welcome uncertainty; anxiety emphasizes possible unwanted outcomes.

face.brows_forehead: Brows may gather during imagined outcomes and loosen when addressed.
face.eyelids: Lids narrow for checking or open at ambiguous signals.
face.gaze: Gaze revisits an information source, clock or person’s response.
face.blink: Clusters of ordinary blinks can mark reorientation after inward attention.
face.cheeks: Cheeks can support a socially reassuring smile that does not last.
face.nose_nostrils: Nose movement is incidental to comfortable breathing, not a signature.
face.lips_mouth: Lips press between questions or prepare an unfinished reassurance.
face.jaw_chin: Jaw may work briefly before a question is allowed out.
face.head_neck: Head tilts to listen for certainty within an ambiguous answer.
face.complexion: No required flush or pallor; retain character and lighting baseline.

voice.pitch_register: Register may sit a little above the character’s settled speaking voice.
voice.pitch_range_contour: Questions can end rising even when grammar is declarative.
voice.loudness: Conversational loudness may persist despite substantial felt intensity.
voice.tempo_rhythm: An even sentence can accelerate through qualifications and conditions.
voice.stress: Stress shifts onto conditional words, deadlines or assurance-seeking details.
voice.articulation: Corrections and precise restatements can replace a first formulation.
voice.resonance: Placement may become light and forward while checking understanding.
voice.texture: Dryness, airiness or a carefully polished tone are optional alternatives.
voice.breath_phrasing: Break speculative chains with comfortable breaths rather than forced breathlessness.
voice.pauses: Pauses invite confirmation or allow a new imagined complication.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A small uncertain laugh or exhale can cover a request for reassurance.

body.head_neck: Head returns toward the same source of information.
body.shoulders: Shoulders adjust repeatedly instead of finding a settled resting place.
body.chest_torso: Torso starts an action, then remains available for interruption.
body.arms_elbows: Elbows may keep work materials close or open for a question.
body.hands_fingers: Fingers check an already arranged object or suspend a routine task.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight transfers can express readiness without requiring pacing.
body.legs_feet: Feet may orient toward the next task before the present one ends.
body.gait: If walking is available, routes may repeat between meaningful checkpoints.
body.proxemics: Distance to a trusted person may decrease during uncertainty.
body.touch_props: A device, list or familiar object can become a checking anchor.
body.stillness: Quietness can contain an active sequence of anticipated possibilities.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: A possibility has become distracting, but ordinary priorities still hold most attention.
levels.face: Let one brow gather while gaze briefly visits the source of uncertainty. Keep lids and cheeks close to baseline. Press the lips after an easy sentence, then release them when the other person offers something concrete.
levels.voice: Use the normal register with a small rising tail on one otherwise ordinary statement. Tone remains clear and volume conversational. Pace briefly slows at the uncertain detail; pause for acknowledgment and take a comfortable breath before returning to the original subject.
levels.body: Continue the existing task while leaving one small part unfinished. Turn the head toward relevant information without rotating the whole torso. Let fingers rest on the object for an extra beat while weight remains comfortably supported.
levels.timing: The concern appears at a transition between tasks and briefly interrupts completion.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the question casual, allowing only the extra wait for an answer to show investment.
levels.recovery: A specific piece of information lets the interrupted task close without further checking.
levels.playable_direction: Find out one small thing so you can get back to what you were doing.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: Several plausible outcomes invite preparation, and reassurance helps only for a while.
levels.face: Bring the brow centers together during inward calculation, then smooth them when making eye contact. Let gaze return to the same device or doorway. A courteous half-smile may precede a question, disappearing while the answer is evaluated.
levels.voice: Let register rise modestly on a checking question, with a lightly tentative tone at ordinary volume. Start at conversational pace, then add a quick qualification. Leave a conspicuous answer-shaped pause and replenish breath comfortably before asking the question in a slightly different form.
levels.body: Arrange a prop twice or review an already completed practical step. Angle the torso toward the information source while one arm continues the social task. Shift seated or standing support when the expected update does not arrive.
levels.timing: Allow reassurance to land, then let a newly noticed exception reopen the concern.
levels.restrained_alternative: Concentrate all visible anxiety into one repeated practical check performed with an otherwise steady face.
levels.recovery: Concrete plans reduce redundant checking before they fully restore ease in conversation.
levels.playable_direction: Make sure the plan still works if that one uncertain detail changes.

levels.label: Clear
levels.felt_state: Uncertainty now competes with the conversation and changes how choices are made.
levels.face: Keep the lower lids engaged while gaze alternates between the speaker and an imagined problem point. Draw the brows on conditional details. Let the lips begin an interruption, close politely, then reopen when a gap permits the question.
levels.voice: Use a slightly raised register and unsettled rising-falling contour while listing possibilities. Tone can be precise but lightly dry, with moderate loudness. Accelerate connecting words, stress the risk-bearing terms, and insert comfortable breaths and checking pauses between scenarios rather than stacking them indefinitely.
levels.body: Pause the original activity to make room for planning. Bring materials within reach, plant the available support and lean the chest toward the answer. A hand may mark two alternatives while the lower body remains ready to resume or redirect.
levels.timing: Each answer is followed by a rapid test against another possible outcome.
levels.restrained_alternative: Let the body remain still while the eyes and exact follow-up questions carry the internal movement.
levels.recovery: An agreed next step permits action even when the uncertainty itself remains unresolved.
levels.playable_direction: Turn the unknown into one manageable next step you can actually take.

levels.label: Strong
levels.felt_state: Anticipated trouble increasingly organizes the scene, making ambiguous signals hard to leave alone.
levels.face: Hold an intent listening expression with gathered brows and narrowed lower lids. Gaze catches small changes in the other person’s face. Let the mouth form a reassuring smile a beat late, then settle into a closed, evaluative line.
levels.voice: Keep register moderately raised or consciously lowered for control; use one rather than both throughout the beat. Tone is tautly careful at restrained conversational volume. Quick speculative clauses alternate with deliberate pauses, and easy breaths separate a question from the reassurance-seeking restatement that follows.
levels.body: Keep the torso forward while a routine action stalls at the hands. Reposition the base toward the next expected event. If movement fits the scene, cross between two meaningful checkpoints; otherwise repeat the check through head orientation alone.
levels.timing: Checking cycles shorten; silence from the information source acquires meaning of its own.
levels.restrained_alternative: Adopt a polished, practical manner whose overprecise sequencing reveals how much uncertainty is being managed.
levels.recovery: Reliable timing information helps the character tolerate a longer interval without checking.
levels.playable_direction: Get a dependable boundary around how long you must keep preparing for this.

levels.label: Intense
levels.felt_state: Possible bad outcomes crowd out neutral explanations, although the character can still collaborate.
levels.face: Let gaze search the speaker’s face for disconfirming evidence, returning repeatedly to the eyes or mouth. The forehead remains gathered between responses. Lips part for several possible questions before one is selected; the chin may lift to request a clear answer.
levels.voice: Use a narrow elevated register with upward hooks on key questions, or a carefully level managed delivery. Keep tone thin but usable and volume recipient-appropriate. Pace quickens through imagined consequences; deliberately pause for the other person and use comfortable shorter breath groups to retain intelligibility.
levels.body: Orient chest and head toward support while elbows gather the practical materials close. Let weight shift with each proposed course of action without completing all of them. One useful task can become the anchor that prevents aimless repeated movement.
levels.timing: Let each new ambiguity interrupt relief before it has fully changed the posture.
levels.restrained_alternative: Contain the scene in a single repeated request delivered quietly, with reduced gestures and sustained listening.
levels.recovery: Collaborative task completion may restore agency sooner than verbal promises restore ease.
levels.playable_direction: Give the other person a specific job that makes waiting feel possible.

levels.label: Consuming
levels.felt_state: The uncertain future occupies most attention; maintaining ordinary interaction requires deliberate effort.
levels.face: Allow the social expression to arrive slowly after inward fixation. Keep brows gathered and lips lightly sealed while gaze lingers on the expected signal. When addressed, return the eyes first, then the head, as though translating from another conversation.
levels.voice: Let register settle into a limited band with occasional upward catches on feared possibilities. Tone may sound carefully smooth over a faint airy edge; volume can stay quiet. Use compressed phrases, longer processing pauses and comfortable breaths, with one clear question emerging from each internal loop.
levels.body: Reduce competing movement and hold the body near the chosen source of certainty. The torso can remain forward over a stable base while hands rest on unused materials. A delayed response to touch or a prop handoff shows attention occupied elsewhere.
levels.timing: External conversation continues while the character repeatedly returns to the same unresolved future moment.
levels.restrained_alternative: Play outward competence with a small delay before every answer that requires leaving the internal scenario.
levels.recovery: Recovery begins when the character can leave one check unfinished without immediately returning to it.
levels.playable_direction: Stay with this person for one answer instead of following the next imagined disaster.

levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: Uncertainty feels all-encompassing; choosing what to attend to becomes the central effort.
levels.face: Use sustained fixation or lowered lids to reduce incoming information, choosing one clear strategy. Brows need not intensify further. The mouth can hold an unfinished response while gaze eventually finds one trusted person, making that small return the central facial event.
levels.voice: Speech may narrow to one question or a request to slow down, in a limited register and low, clear tone. Avoid equating intensity with loudness. Let pace become deliberately sparse, pauses carry the struggle to select information, and comfortable breaths support one complete thought at a time.
levels.body: Choose a stable supported position and remove unnecessary tasks from the body. Arms may rest while the chest turns toward one source of guidance. If movement resumes, let it follow a single agreed instruction rather than attempting every anticipated contingency.
levels.timing: Suspend the checking cycle long enough for one piece of information to be received fully.
levels.restrained_alternative: A still, ordinary-looking posture can house overwhelming anticipation; show it through delayed selective responses.
levels.recovery: One tolerable action restores contact with the present before wider planning becomes available again.
levels.playable_direction: Let one reliable fact be enough for the next few seconds.

variants.label: Awaiting evaluation
variants.context: A result or judgment matters, and the character cannot yet know how they were received.
variants.objective: Get usable feedback without surrendering dignity.
variants.face_modifier: Read evaluators’ small reactions rather than scanning for physical danger.
variants.voice_modifier: Let questions hide inside reasonable requests for process information.
variants.body_modifier: Use papers, clothing or presentation materials as plausible preparation anchors.
variants.timing_modifier: Concern returns during unanswered gaps.

seven_levels.modifier: Check the evaluator’s reaction after a routine remark, then resume the prepared material before the glance becomes conspicuous.
Adjust one already adequate detail while asking when feedback will arrive, letting the practical question carry the need for certainty.
Rehearse a possible explanation internally, then choose a neutral question that tests whether an error was actually noticed.
Watch a minor facial change as though it could settle the whole result; keep the prepared social smile a beat late.
Ask for a concrete criterion when reassurance feels too vague, allowing urgency into the precision rather than the volume.
Continue familiar procedural tasks correctly while attention repeatedly returns to the unanswered question of how you were judged.
Reduce the interaction to one request for clear next steps; accepting that instruction becomes the first manageable return to action.

variants.label: Waiting for news
variants.context: The character awaits information about a valued person or uncertain event.
variants.objective: Stay reachable and gain an update that can be trusted.
variants.face_modifier: Return gaze to the actual news channel, then to anyone sharing the wait.
variants.voice_modifier: Use compact checking questions and let silence after them remain consequential.
variants.body_modifier: Keep a device accessible without requiring repetitive tapping or pacing.
variants.timing_modifier: Every update starts a fresh appraisal rather than resolving all uncertainty.

seven_levels.modifier: Notice the device during conversation, then leave it alone while one sentence finishes; the waiting remains peripheral.
Check whether the sound or signal was real, letting a small disappointed reset follow an irrelevant notification.
Ask when the next update should come and orient the body toward remaining available until then.
Let a partial update briefly loosen the face before one unresolved detail draws the brows together again.
Coordinate one practical task with another person while returning to the information channel whenever the task pauses.

Choose one person to interpret the next update; focus on their face long enough to receive one complete piece of information.

temporal_arc.onset: An unresolved possibility intrudes into otherwise workable activity.
temporal_arc.escalation: Monitoring and preparation bring temporary control, followed by another qualification.
temporal_arc.apex: The effort to manage uncertainty becomes more demanding than the original task.
temporal_arc.recovery: A concrete next step or tolerable uncertainty permits attention to return to the present.
temporal_arc.carryover: The character may keep a reminder, checking habit or greater sensitivity to ambiguous delays.

transitions.trigger: A concrete immediate threat emerges from the uncertainty.
transitions.bridge: Replace broad checking with a fixed target and a usable protective instruction.

transitions.trigger: Reliable information removes a feared possibility.
transitions.bridge: Let the answer register in the eyes before questions cease and phrasing lengthens.

transitions.trigger: Attention settles into repeated verbal rehearsal of the same possibilities.
transitions.bridge: Reduce outward searching while increasingly elaborate conditional sentences continue the concern.

prompt_example.spoken_text: I thought you would be here.
prompt_example.visual_direction: Keep the eyes returning to the silent phone; offer the listener a small social smile that fades while awaiting their answer.
prompt_example.delivery_direction: Use an ordinary volume with a rising edge on “here”; pause as though their presence would have made the uncertainty manageable.

cue_conflicts: Anxiety may be physically restless or highly contained; select the strategy that serves the scene.
A fluent, organized voice does not disprove intense internal anxiety.
Information seeking can be sensible preparation; repetition becomes meaningful only against context and baseline.
emotions.context_notes: This is a playable affective state, not an anxiety-disorder label. Calibrate checking against the actual uncertainty, role, power and relationship. Cultural display conventions and individual habits matter; use gaze, object placement or seated weight changes when pacing is unavailable.

emotions.label: Dread
emotions.definition: Anticipatory distress organized around an approaching unwanted event that feels difficult to avoid. The future is experienced as drawing nearer rather than merely possible.
emotions.appraisal: That unwanted moment is coming, and I cannot find a convincing way to keep it from reaching me.
emotions.objective: Delay, prepare for or gain companionship through the approaching event while preserving some choice about meeting it.
action_tendencies: Postpone the next step toward the event.
Track time or signs of approach.
Seek company or a practical buffer.
Prepare reluctantly for what feels unavoidable.
distinctions: Anxiety emphasizes unresolved possibilities; dread often has a specific expected event.
Despair emphasizes unavailable improvement; dread can coexist with a workable response to what is coming.
Fear may concern present danger; dread gives the approaching future a heavy presence.

face.brows_forehead: Brows can draw inward and remain there between external cues.
face.eyelids: Upper lids may lower until a sign of arrival lifts them.
face.gaze: Gaze rests on the route, clock or object associated with what is coming.
face.blink: Blinks can punctuate reluctant returns from imagining the event.
face.cheeks: Cheeks may lose their social animation without becoming uniformly slack.
face.nose_nostrils: No fixed nostril pattern is necessary.
face.lips_mouth: Lips close after an unfinished objection or reluctant agreement.
face.jaw_chin: Jaw can settle heavily or briefly brace before the next step.
face.head_neck: Head may incline away while eyes remain on the approaching cue.
face.complexion: Color is not an intensity measure; maintain lighting continuity.

voice.pitch_register: Register can move toward the character’s lower comfortable range.
voice.pitch_range_contour: Contours may fall early, with a rise only at a possible reprieve.
voice.loudness: Volume often reduces as the event occupies attention.
voice.tempo_rhythm: Starts can be delayed; necessary practical words may then arrive quickly.
voice.stress: Stress may land on temporal words such as now, tomorrow or again.
voice.articulation: Articulation can remain exact around reluctance rather than becoming uniformly slurred.
voice.resonance: Resonance may feel less outwardly projected or deliberately matter-of-fact.
voice.texture: A dry, weighted or carefully neutral tone is a selectable texture.
voice.breath_phrasing: Let comfortable exhaled phrases finish without manufacturing depletion.
voice.pauses: Pauses often precede commitment or acknowledgment of the deadline.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A quiet exhale or reluctant hum can acknowledge the approaching obligation.

body.head_neck: Head can turn last when the next step is announced.
body.shoulders: Shoulders may settle as postponement runs out.
body.chest_torso: Torso remains oriented away from the object that initiates the event.
body.arms_elbows: Arms may delay releasing a protective or familiar position.
body.hands_fingers: Hands linger on the last ordinary task before departure.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight stays on the support farthest from the required movement.
body.legs_feet: Feet may remain planted after the upper body agrees to go.
body.gait: A measured start can contrast with automatic practical movement afterward.
body.proxemics: Closeness to trusted company may temporarily make waiting tolerable.
body.touch_props: Coats, keys or documents can mark the unwanted threshold.
body.stillness: Stillness can preserve the imagined time before the event begins.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: An approaching obligation puts a shadow across an otherwise ordinary moment.
levels.face: Let gaze touch the relevant object and stay one beat longer than necessary. Draw the inner brows slightly, then restore the listening face. Close the lips on a small exhale while the chin remains oriented toward the present company.
levels.voice: Use a comfortable register with an early downward contour on the event’s mention. Tone stays clear and quiet-conversational. Delay the first word, then speak at normal pace; leave a short pause before the time reference and replenish breath naturally before changing subjects.
levels.body: Allow one routine action to slow at its final step. Keep the torso with the current activity while the head acknowledges the future demand. Let weight remain comfortably settled instead of preparing immediately to leave.
levels.timing: The feeling surfaces when the event is named, then recedes behind the current activity.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the face ordinary and place the entire beat in reluctance to finish a small task.
levels.recovery: A welcome distraction restores present engagement until the next reminder of the event.
levels.playable_direction: Keep this ordinary moment going a little longer before thinking about what comes next.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: The unwanted event feels close enough to influence small decisions about time.
levels.face: Look toward the clock or entry route, then lower the gaze to the unfinished task. Let the brow centers remain drawn during that return. Lips press before a polite acknowledgment; the jaw releases only when the subject moves away.
levels.voice: Let register sit slightly lower with a flat opening and falling end. Tone can be dry but unforced, at modest volume. Slow around the agreement, use one practical phrase at normal pace, and place an easy breath and pause before admitting when the event happens.
levels.body: Keep an ordinary prop in use after its purpose is complete. Turn the chest only partly toward departure or preparation. Place feet or available support securely as though the current position still has a task to justify it.
levels.timing: Use small postponements that each seem reasonable until their shared direction becomes apparent.
levels.restrained_alternative: Agree verbally at once while letting the body take an extra beat to begin.
levels.recovery: A specific preparation step can convert waiting into bounded, tolerable action.
levels.playable_direction: Find one reasonable thing that still needs doing before you have to face it.

levels.label: Clear
levels.felt_state: The event feels inevitable enough that the character starts budgeting emotional effort for it.
levels.face: Hold gaze on the approaching cue, with upper lids lowered until a new sound briefly opens them. Gather the brows without a continuous grimace. Let the mouth shape a question about delay, then close when the answer seems known.
levels.voice: Use a lower settled register and restrained contour, with a small lift on any possible reprieve. Tone is weighted or carefully plain at low conversational volume. Speak in measured clauses, pause before accepting the next step, and let comfortable breathing separate practical preparation from personal admission.
levels.body: Gather necessary objects while keeping the torso slightly turned away from the threshold. Elbows remain near the body; hands perform a familiar sequence with less flourish. Shift weight only after the last possible practical excuse has been completed.
levels.timing: Preparation advances while emotional commitment lags one beat behind each completed action.
levels.restrained_alternative: Play meticulous efficiency with a delayed look at the object that makes the event real.
levels.recovery: Companionship or a clear plan allows forward movement while the unwanted anticipation remains.
levels.playable_direction: Prepare everything you can control so you do not have to imagine the rest.

levels.label: Strong
levels.felt_state: The approaching moment weighs on the present, making delay both tempting and conspicuous.
levels.face: Keep the brows knitted through ordinary conversation and let gaze repeatedly leave for the route of arrival. Lips can hold an interrupted objection. Raise the chin briefly to accept reassurance, then let it settle when the same deadline returns to attention.
levels.voice: Begin low in the comfortable register with a near-level contour; let a proposed escape briefly raise it. Tone may be muted and edged with dry humor, at contained loudness. Allow longer onset pauses, compact practical bursts and easy breaths before the words that commit the character.
levels.body: Lean away from the initiating object without retreating from the listener. Keep one arm connected to a familiar surface or companion if welcome. The lower body waits while the upper body performs readiness, creating a clear split between agreement and departure.
levels.timing: A momentary reprieve produces a visible lift that falls when its limitation is understood.
levels.restrained_alternative: Hold a steady social face while every movement toward the event begins later than expected.
levels.recovery: Relief from delay may be temporary; genuine recovery needs a changed appraisal or completed encounter.
levels.playable_direction: Test whether there is still a way to postpone this without saying you cannot bear it.

levels.label: Intense
levels.felt_state: The future event dominates perception; neutral details begin to feel like countdown markers.
levels.face: Fix gaze on the sound source, envelope or doorway that will announce the next stage. The forehead stays drawn while the cheeks lose conversational animation. Let lips part on a private objection, then deliberately form the socially required answer.
levels.voice: Use a narrow lower register with a small break in contour when the event becomes immediate. Tone can sound hollow or deliberately factual, with modest loudness. Slow at the threshold phrase, pause afterward, and use comfortable short breath groups for necessities rather than forcing a long depleted delivery.
levels.body: Hold the body near a trusted anchor while practical readiness accumulates around it. Hands may finish packing or fastening, but torso and pelvis remain reluctant to orient toward departure. Let the first committed shift carry more significance than larger decorative movement.
levels.timing: Each signal of approach interrupts the current action before the signal is fully identified.
levels.restrained_alternative: Perform the required sequence correctly with almost no facial display, reserving one delayed gaze for the threshold.
levels.recovery: Crossing into the event may replace anticipation with concrete coping before any sense of safety returns.
levels.playable_direction: Get to the first actual step without living through the whole event in advance.

levels.label: Consuming
levels.felt_state: Almost everything in the present is experienced in relation to the unwanted moment ahead.
levels.face: Choose sustained downward gaze that lifts only for arrival cues, or fixed watching of the threshold. Keep the mouth in a small unfinished shape before each answer. Let the jaw settle after recognition, as though another avenue of postponement has quietly closed.
levels.voice: Keep register compressed and contour economical, with a quiet, weighted tone. Loudness can remain intimate even when stakes are extreme. Necessary words may arrive abruptly after long pauses; take comfortable breaths at those gaps and leave optional explanations unsaid rather than artificially stretching every syllable.
levels.body: Choose a supported still position with the body turned toward one source of companionship. Release unnecessary props. The hand may remain on a coat or bag without lifting it, while the base postpones the movement that would acknowledge the next stage.
levels.timing: Lengthen the beat between knowing it is time and allowing the first committed movement.
levels.restrained_alternative: Let a calm, ordinary reply conceal the dread; reveal it only when the reply fails to initiate action.
levels.recovery: A trusted person’s concrete accompaniment can restore movement before dread meaningfully diminishes.
levels.playable_direction: Ask someone to stay through the next minute without having to explain the entire fear.

levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: The approaching event fills experience so completely that the next voluntary step becomes the dramatic task.
levels.face: Let the face grow still around a fixed or lowered gaze; escalation need not add more muscle movement. A tiny lift of the inner brows can meet the person offering help. Keep the lips closed until one necessary answer can be chosen.
levels.voice: Use one quiet phrase in a comfortable low or middle register, with little melodic movement. Tone may be plain rather than audibly distressed. Pace becomes sparse, pauses hold the burden of commitment, and each naturally replenished breath supports only the words needed to permit the next step.
levels.body: Ground the body in available support and reduce action to one reachable choice. Head and torso may turn toward a companion before the rest follows. If locomotion occurs, make its initiation deliberate and safe; stillness can remain the primary expression.
levels.timing: Let one meaningful invitation create the opening for action; repeated countdown gestures are unnecessary.
levels.restrained_alternative: Outward readiness can be complete while the withheld first step shows overwhelming inward resistance.
levels.recovery: Recovery begins with meeting one concrete part of the event, then reassessing what is actually happening.
levels.playable_direction: Allow yourself to take only this next step, with someone beside you if possible.

variants.label: Scheduled confrontation
variants.context: A known meeting, disclosure or difficult conversation is approaching.
variants.objective: Arrive with enough agency to say the essential thing.
variants.face_modifier: Give the clock and meeting materials a recurring but economical place in gaze.
variants.voice_modifier: Let practical scheduling language carry the reluctance.
variants.body_modifier: Prepare the meeting objects while delaying the movement that begins it.
variants.timing_modifier: Distinguish preparation beats from the final threshold beat.

seven_levels.modifier: Notice the appointment while finishing a pleasant exchange, letting one brief downward contour mark the reminder.
Ask about a small logistical detail that might create extra time before the meeting begins.
Practice the opening phrase silently, then return to arranging the papers rather than beginning the encounter.
Accept reassurance politely while keeping attention on the door through which the other person will arrive.
Complete all practical preparation and confront the fact that no remaining task can delay the opening sentence.
Let the arrival sound halt the hands; find one trusted face before turning toward the person you must address.
Permit one word or one movement across the threshold to begin the encounter; the dread remains present during that choice.

variants.label: Awaiting an unwanted recurrence
variants.context: A familiar difficult event appears likely to happen again.
variants.objective: Find a different way through a situation whose pattern feels recognizable.
variants.face_modifier: Let recognition precede the larger reaction; gaze can anticipate the next familiar cue.
variants.voice_modifier: Use a tired knowing contour without making the whole voice exhausted.
variants.body_modifier: Position familiar protective or comforting resources before they are requested.
variants.timing_modifier: React to precursors because the character remembers the sequence.

seven_levels.modifier: Recognize the first familiar sign while others continue normally; let a brief stilling of the mouth carry the private association.
Place one useful item within reach because experience suggests it will be needed, keeping the movement ordinary.
Ask whether this time will be different, allowing the question to contain both practical inquiry and remembered disappointment.
Watch the next familiar step occur and let the possibility of reprieve recede without requiring a dramatic facial collapse.
Interrupt the known sequence with one concrete request, giving the effort more urgency than the outward volume.
Seek a witness or companion before the next stage, making shared presence the remaining change available to you.
Choose one different response within the recurring event; a tiny deliberate deviation becomes the scene’s entire expression of agency.

temporal_arc.onset: A reminder places an unwanted future event inside the present scene.
temporal_arc.escalation: Signs of approach remove opportunities for delay or imagined reprieve.
temporal_arc.apex: The threshold becomes immediate and initiating action feels disproportionately difficult.
temporal_arc.recovery: The actual encounter supplies concrete information and a sequence of manageable responses.
temporal_arc.carryover: Future reminders may acquire weight, while successfully endured details can become resources.

transitions.trigger: The anticipated threat becomes immediately present.
transitions.bridge: Lift attention from the countdown to a concrete target and choose a protective response.

transitions.trigger: The event is canceled, changed or safely completed.
transitions.bridge: Verify the change before letting the body stop organizing around the threshold.

transitions.trigger: The character chooses a reason to meet the event despite dread.
transitions.bridge: Let gaze settle on the purpose and permit the first intentional forward action.

prompt_example.spoken_text: I thought you would be here.
prompt_example.visual_direction: Look at the unopened door before looking at the listener; keep the packed bag resting where it has been for several beats.
prompt_example.delivery_direction: Deliver the line quietly with weight on “would”; pause before “be here” as though companionship had been part of the plan.

cue_conflicts: Dread can slow action while leaving thought fast; do not automatically slow every channel together.
A familiar event may produce dry humor rather than a uniformly solemn face.
Crossing the threshold may increase dread or replace it with practical fear; choose the scene’s actual turn.
emotions.context_notes: Use the event’s personal meaning and actual options, not a universal prediction of harm. Relationship and power determine whether postponement can be spoken openly. Cultural conventions and mobility affect threshold behavior; a gaze shift or consent to begin can replace walking.

emotions.label: Panic
emotions.definition: An acute configuration of alarm in which the character feels that available coping or escape is failing. This performance label describes a moment in a story, not a diagnosis or required bodily syndrome.
emotions.appraisal: Danger feels urgent and I cannot readily organize a reliable response.
emotions.objective: Find one usable point of safety, help or direction amid perceived loss of control.
action_tendencies: Search urgently for an exit or assistance.
Repeat a failed attempt before changing strategy.
Freeze when too many actions compete.
Follow one clear instruction when it becomes available.
distinctions: Fear can remain organized around effective protection; panic foregrounds difficulty organizing coping.
High excitement also accelerates behavior but does not center perceived urgent danger.
Overwhelming intensity does not require a clinical panic attack or visible collapse.

face.brows_forehead: Brows may rise and draw together during failed attempts.
face.eyelids: Eyes may open wide or narrow to exclude distracting input.
face.gaze: Gaze can jump among options before finding one anchor.
face.blink: Blink timing may interrupt scanning or accompany a reset.
face.cheeks: Cheeks brace around an incomplete word or urgent appeal.
face.nose_nostrils: Use comfortable breathing; nostril flare is never obligatory.
face.lips_mouth: Mouth starts instructions, questions or calls that may change midway.
face.jaw_chin: Jaw can briefly brace before an abandoned phrase.
face.head_neck: Head turns toward new options faster than the torso follows.
face.complexion: No required color change or presumed physiological diagnosis.

voice.pitch_register: Register may jump unexpectedly relative to the character’s baseline.
voice.pitch_range_contour: Contour can restart upward as each new option is proposed.
voice.loudness: Volume may spike, remain whispered or become carefully restrained.
voice.tempo_rhythm: Fast attempts can alternate with abrupt blank intervals.
voice.stress: Stress falls on immediate action words or a helper’s name.
voice.articulation: Restarts can interrupt an otherwise intelligible essential word.
voice.resonance: A forward compact sound can help short urgent messages carry.
voice.texture: Airy, rough-edged or unusually plain tones are optional choices.
voice.breath_phrasing: Use short comfortable phrases; never perform forced hyperventilation.
voice.pauses: Gaps can mark searching, listening or difficulty selecting action.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A brief cry, gasp-like acted sound or wordless appeal is optional.

body.head_neck: Head may search before choosing one reliable direction.
body.shoulders: Shoulders gather for protection or release during guided action.
body.chest_torso: Torso can start toward one option then check itself.
body.arms_elbows: Arms may begin competing actions before one becomes useful.
body.hands_fingers: Hands abandon ineffective handling and seek a stable contact.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight transfers may hesitate between incompatible directions.
body.legs_feet: Feet or mobility support need safe placement despite acted urgency.
body.gait: Movement can be rapid, interrupted or completely inhibited.
body.proxemics: Closeness to a helper may become a practical orientation point.
body.touch_props: A prop may be repeatedly tried until attention accepts another method.
body.stillness: Sudden stillness can show overload rather than calm.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: Alarm briefly outruns the character’s ability to choose the next response.
levels.face: Lift the brows and open the lids at the failed first option. Let gaze jump once to an alternative. The mouth begins a second instruction before the first has finished; close it briefly to select a usable word.
levels.voice: Let register jump on the opening word, then return toward baseline with a questioning contour. Tone is clear but hurried, at moderate loudness. Restart one short phrase, pause to locate the answer, and take an easy breath before completing the practical request.
levels.body: Start one useful action, interrupt it and choose another without losing safe support. Head turns ahead of the chest. Hands hover briefly between two tasks while pelvis and feet remain available to follow the selected option.
levels.timing: Place the small disorganization immediately after a plan unexpectedly fails.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the body still and expose the moment through one repeated question.
levels.recovery: One clear answer restores sequence before the underlying danger is resolved.
levels.playable_direction: Find the next workable action before this interruption becomes a larger problem.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: An urgent problem produces competing actions and a stronger need for guidance.
levels.face: Gather the inner brows while gaze alternates between the obstruction and a potential helper. Lids remain alert. Let the lips repeat the beginning of a word, then press together while the jaw prepares a more direct request.
levels.voice: Use a lifted register with a rising restart and a firmer falling request. Tone may have a light airy edge; keep volume suited to distance. Pace accelerates through options, then stops for an answer; separate attempts with comfortable breaths instead of a continuous rushed stream.
levels.body: Reposition the chest toward help while one hand remains on the failed task. Let elbows release that task only after the answer registers. Establish the base first, then redirect the body, showing urgency through sequencing rather than unsafe movement.
levels.timing: Two quick failed attempts precede a deliberate effort to hear another person.
levels.restrained_alternative: Ask quietly and precisely while the eyes keep returning to the failed option.
levels.recovery: Following one instruction restores a small sense of control and steadies the hands.
levels.playable_direction: Get someone to give you one instruction you can trust right now.

levels.label: Clear
levels.felt_state: Coping feels unreliable enough that the character starts repeating rather than adapting.
levels.face: Keep gaze returning to the same blocked route despite noticing alternatives. Raise and gather brows on each failed try. The mouth stays prepared to call, then closes briefly when the helper demands attention; the chin turns toward that voice last.
levels.voice: Use a variable register with repeated upward launches on the same request. Tone can be thin or insistently clear, with uneven but controlled volume. Quick phrases recur at similar rhythm; insert a real listening pause and a comfortable breath when another person offers direction.
levels.body: Repeat one safe practical action once, then let the hand suspend above it. The torso leans toward the obstruction while the head turns to help. Shift the available support only when the new direction is understood.
levels.timing: Let repetition reveal the narrowing options; a helper’s intervention briefly interrupts the loop.
levels.restrained_alternative: Play quiet repetition with limited gesture, making the unchanged request more revealing than loudness.
levels.recovery: A successful small action breaks the loop and allows the next instruction to land.
levels.playable_direction: Stop trying the same thing long enough to hear a usable alternative.

levels.label: Strong
levels.felt_state: Urgency fragments the plan, and holding attention on one person becomes difficult.
levels.face: Let the eyes search rapidly among meaningful targets, then struggle to stay on the helper. Brows remain lifted and drawn. Lips form two competing responses before one emerges; keep cheeks braced only during the effort to make that word clear.
levels.voice: Choose an elevated register with abrupt contour resets, or a deliberately compressed whisper when concealment matters. Tone is urgent and lightly uneven. Volume follows context; fast fragments alternate with listening gaps, and comfortable breaths support single instructions instead of forced breathlessness or sustained yelling.
levels.body: Begin to turn the torso toward one route, stop, then settle onto stable support. One arm may reach toward help while the other releases an unnecessary prop. Keep lower-body movement simple enough that the attention shifts remain the main choreography.
levels.timing: Every new cue threatens to interrupt the response before it is completed.
levels.restrained_alternative: Let a fixed posture contain the panic while speech repeatedly loses its intended sequence.
levels.recovery: Retain one helper, one task and one completed movement before adding more information.
levels.playable_direction: Keep your attention on the person who can help you finish this one action.

levels.label: Intense
levels.felt_state: The character experiences immediate danger and can sustain only a very narrow plan.
levels.face: Anchor gaze on one face or escape point after an unmistakable search. Let brows hold high or tight, with lips parted around an unfinished appeal. A brief jaw tremor is optional; the essential change is that other faces stop receiving full acknowledgment.
levels.voice: Keep register in a narrow urgent band with one upward break on the needed name. Tone may be fragile or sharply plain; loudness can remain low. Use brief clear words, uneven pauses and easy breaths, allowing the effort to understand a response to slow the next utterance.
levels.body: Let the body gather around a single anchor: supported sitting, a stable surface or a helper’s offered hand. Reduce prop manipulation. Align chest and pelvis with the selected task while the head remains available for the one instruction that matters.
levels.timing: The search contracts into a single point of contact that must be repeatedly regained.
levels.restrained_alternative: Use almost motionless urgency and one quiet recurring word instead of visible frantic activity.
levels.recovery: A completed instruction earns a short orientation pause before any new demand is introduced.
levels.playable_direction: Let this one voice become the path through the noise of competing possibilities.

levels.label: Consuming
levels.felt_state: The sense of losing control consumes attention; speech or movement may become strongly inhibited.
levels.face: Choose fixed wide attention or protective lowered lids, according to the character’s coping strategy. Brows need not grow more dramatic. Hold the mouth on an unspoken word, then let gaze return to the helper in one small, deliberate movement.
levels.voice: Speech can shrink to a name or affirmative syllable in a limited register and quiet, clear tone. Keep volume independent of intensity. Long selection pauses separate words; natural easy breaths continue, and a helper’s cadence can provide the rhythm for one intelligible response at a time.
levels.body: Maintain a supported position while unnecessary actions cease. Let arms rest or hold a useful stable contact, with torso angled toward guidance. A single nod, hand release or weight adjustment may represent substantial regained capacity without requiring a full-body reaction.
levels.timing: Expand the gap between receiving an instruction and being able to act on it.
levels.restrained_alternative: A composed outer face can accompany delayed comprehension and a very small available action.
levels.recovery: Recovery begins with orientation and one voluntary response, not an instant return to effortless conversation.
levels.playable_direction: Find the smallest response that lets someone know you can still follow them.

levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: Almost all attention is absorbed by urgent alarm; only a minimal organizing cue feels usable.
levels.face: Let the expression remain suspended rather than escalating into a larger mask. Keep gaze fixed, closed or narrowly anchored as a chosen alternative. One change at the mouth or brows marks recognition when a trusted person reaches the character’s attention.
levels.voice: Use silence or a single quiet word in a comfortable register, with little contour. If speech returns, keep tone plain and volume small, pace sparse and pauses long enough for actual processing. Let ordinary breathing continue without instructing gasping, breath holding or forced vocal strain.
levels.body: Choose stable stillness, a sustained protective position or one guided action. Keep safe physical support clear. The body need not collapse; a small head turn or release of an unnecessary grip can be the first visible sign that agency is returning.
levels.timing: Hold the apex around limited responsiveness until one specific cue changes what the character can do.
levels.restrained_alternative: Play the entire peak through silence and delayed eye contact while maintaining an ordinary supported posture.
levels.recovery: Return in steps: recognize a person, receive a simple fact, complete one chosen action.
levels.playable_direction: Allow one trustworthy signal to reach you and answer it in the smallest possible way.

variants.label: Blocked escape
variants.context: An expected route or method of leaving no longer works.
variants.objective: Find another safe option and commit to it.
variants.face_modifier: Keep the blocked option as an early gaze magnet, then transfer attention deliberately.
variants.voice_modifier: Let repeated location words give way to one new direction.
variants.body_modifier: Abandon the failed prop or route when the new plan registers.
variants.timing_modifier: The scene turns when repetition becomes adaptation.

seven_levels.modifier: Try the expected route, register the failure and glance for another opening before making a second attempt.
Ask whether the obstruction can be changed while the hand remains poised to retry the original method.
Repeat the ineffective action once, then let another person’s specific instruction interrupt the pattern.
Look past several options without selecting until one clear landmark makes the alternative concrete.
Commit attention to one new route and let the first completed movement carry more meaning than further searching.
Accept a single guided adjustment while maintaining stable support; changing direction is the whole available task.
Let recognition of a helper or usable opening produce only a small voluntary response before larger movement becomes possible.

variants.label: Losing contact with someone
variants.context: The character cannot locate or reach a person whose safety matters.
variants.objective: Establish contact or obtain one reliable location.
variants.face_modifier: Search faces and routes for the specific person rather than indiscriminate visual agitation.
variants.voice_modifier: Use the person’s name as a practical address, not a mandatory shouted refrain.
variants.body_modifier: Keep communication tools usable and free one hand for useful action.
variants.timing_modifier: Failed contact attempts create distinct beats.

seven_levels.modifier: Check the expected location and let a quick second look interrupt the ordinary greeting.
Call once at recipient-appropriate volume, then pause long enough to genuinely listen for a response.
Retry one contact method before asking another person for a concrete observation about where the missing person went.

temporal_arc.onset: An urgent cue coincides with a failure of the expected coping response.
temporal_arc.escalation: Repeated attempts, competing plans or narrowed attention reduce organized action.
temporal_arc.apex: Alarm dominates and behavior may become frantic, repetitive or inhibited.
temporal_arc.recovery: A trustworthy cue and one manageable action rebuild sequence.
temporal_arc.carryover: Relief, fatigue, embarrassment, anger or continued fear may follow; none is automatic.

transitions.trigger: One workable protective plan restores organized coping while danger remains.
transitions.bridge: Let gaze stay on one target and complete an instruction without restarting.

transitions.trigger: Verified safety or contact removes the immediate emergency.
transitions.bridge: Allow recognition first, then less urgent pacing and broader attention.

transitions.trigger: The character shifts into reduced felt access after overwhelming alarm.
transitions.bridge: Let repeated searching cease and replies become remote rather than treating quietness as relief.

prompt_example.spoken_text: I thought you would be here.
prompt_example.visual_direction: Find the listener’s face after a brief search; start to speak, stop and make the next attempt a clear request for contact.
prompt_example.delivery_direction: Let the first words launch quickly in a lifted register; slow “be here” into a quieter appeal with an easy breath afterward.

cue_conflicts: Rapid action and inhibited stillness are alternative panic presentations, not a required sequence.
Do not direct actual hyperventilation, dangerous breath holding or vocal strain to simulate alarm.
Panic is a story-state label here; no cue establishes a medical event or diagnosis.
emotions.context_notes: Build from the character’s coping history, immediate danger and available help. Power and relationship affect whether requests can be explicit. Culture and mobility shape visible options; urgent eye contact, delayed selection or assisted action can replace pacing and running.

emotions.label: Horror
emotions.definition: A mixed response to something experienced as profoundly terrible, violating or difficult to assimilate, often combining fear, aversion, shock and concern for others.
emotions.appraisal: What I am seeing or understanding crosses a boundary of what should be happening, and I cannot easily take it in.
emotions.objective: Recognize what has happened, establish distance or protection, and decide whether witnessing or intervention is possible.
action_tendencies: Look away, then check the reality of the event.
Reject, question or bear witness to what occurred.
distinctions: Fear centers danger and protection; horror can persist while the witness is physically safe.
Disgust centers aversion or rejection; horror may foreground terrible meaning and human consequences.
Surprise registers unexpectedness without requiring the event to be appalling.

face.brows_forehead: Brows may lift centrally before drawing together in disbelief.
face.eyelids: Lids can widen at recognition or close to interrupt viewing.
face.gaze: Gaze may fix on one detail, then avoid the whole scene.
face.blink: A delayed blink can end an unassimilated stare.
face.cheeks: Cheeks may brace beneath the eyes during rejection.
face.nose_nostrils: Nose can wrinkle if aversion is foregrounded, but need not.
face.lips_mouth: Lips part on recognition or seal against an immediate response.
face.jaw_chin: Jaw may drop briefly, then set to enable action.
face.head_neck: Head retracts or turns away while attention remains captured.
face.complexion: No fixed pallor, flushing or other color signature.

voice.pitch_register: Register may rise on disbelief or lower after comprehension.
voice.pitch_range_contour: A suspended contour can precede a decisive rejecting fall.
voice.loudness: Volume may reduce sharply rather than increase.
voice.tempo_rhythm: A halted start can give way to precise, deliberate statements.
voice.stress: Stress identifies the terrible detail or violated boundary.
voice.articulation: Words may be carefully separated to make the event nameable.
voice.resonance: Resonance may seem less projected during initial disbelief.
voice.texture: A hushed, dry or lightly unsteady tone is optional.
voice.breath_phrasing: Use easy short phrases during recognition; avoid forced gasps.
voice.pauses: Long pauses can represent assimilation rather than empty dramatic emphasis.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A quiet exclamation or involuntary-seeming sound may precede language.

body.head_neck: Head may retract before the body changes position.
body.shoulders: Shoulders can guard the upper torso without a sustained hunch.
body.chest_torso: Chest draws away, then may reorient toward a person needing help.
body.arms_elbows: Arms can halt an approach or shield another viewer.
body.hands_fingers: Hands stop a task, cover a prop or reach toward assistance.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight shifts back or remains fixed in witness-like stillness.
body.legs_feet: Feet select safe support before any retreat or approach.
body.gait: Movement can stop at the threshold of comprehension.
body.proxemics: Distance may increase from the event while decreasing toward another person.
body.touch_props: An object can be set down because it suddenly feels inappropriate.
body.stillness: Stillness can express witnessing something not yet assimilated.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: A disturbing detail unsettles the scene before its full meaning is understood.
levels.face: Pause the gaze on one detail and lift the inner brows. Let the lips part slightly, then close as the eyes check the larger context. Keep the jaw usable; one delayed blink can mark the first attempt to dismiss the impression.
levels.voice: Use baseline register with a small upward contour on the questioning word. Tone becomes quieter and drier than the preceding conversation. Slow the phrase, pause to look again and take an easy breath before asking for clarification, leaving loudness restrained rather than signaling full alarm.
levels.body: Stop a casual approach or prop action midway. Let the head remain oriented toward the detail while the torso begins a small withdrawal. Keep the existing support stable and allow the hands to finish only after the meaning is checked.
levels.timing: Recognition develops after the interrupted action, not before the character could know what was seen.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the face socially composed and let the unfinished action carry the disturbance.
levels.recovery: A benign explanation restores the interrupted task, perhaps with a final verifying glance.
levels.playable_direction: Check whether you really saw what you think you saw.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: The disturbing meaning appears credible, provoking aversion and a need to confirm it.
levels.face: Draw the brows after the initial lift and narrow the lower lids toward the detail. Let the mouth open for a question that comes late. Gaze briefly leaves, then returns deliberately; the chin withdraws without a theatrical full-head recoil.
levels.voice: Let register lift on disbelief and fall at the end of the confirmation question. Use a hushed, clear tone at reduced conversational volume. Separate the crucial words, pause for the answer and replenish breath naturally before naming the detail that makes the interpretation difficult to accept.
levels.body: Bring the torso slightly away while keeping the head available to witness. One hand may release an ordinary object onto a surface. Shift the base toward a position that permits either further observation or a protective approach if the meaning is confirmed.
levels.timing: The return look carries the decision to know rather than merely the reflex to see.
levels.restrained_alternative: Use a level factual question with one small backward weight shift and a fixed gaze.
levels.recovery: Clarification may settle uncertainty while leaving the appalled response intact.
levels.playable_direction: Get someone to confirm the detail you wish you had misunderstood.
