levels.felt_state: The target’s presence occupies attention even when direct contact is avoidable.
levels.face: Eyes return to the target after attempted disengagement. The brow holds a fixed crease, lips press before any mention of the name, and the jaw releases slowly as the character redirects attention to present company.
levels.voice: Use a narrow lower register with isolated emphatic rises on the target’s influence. Tone is hard or bitter, volume controlled; pace becomes exact and repetitive, pauses interrupt attempted normal talk, and ordinary breath resets help separate the grievance from the current task.
levels.body: Keep the body oriented toward valued people while attention pulls back toward the target. Hands tighten then release around a safe prop, the torso turns only partway, and weight stays near the chosen boundary.
levels.timing: The target need not act; reminders now interrupt unrelated activity.
levels.restrained_alternative: Remain outwardly helpful while repeatedly checking whether the target can affect the outcome.
levels.recovery: A meaningful separation can reduce preoccupation; the stance may survive the calmer body.
levels.playable_direction: Protect your life from being organized around their presence.

face.text: Return the gaze to the target after attempting to disengage.
Hold a fixed crease as the target occupies unwanted attention.
Press the lips before naming the target's renewed influence.

voice.text: Keep lower pitch narrow with isolated rises on consequential details.
Use a hard or bitter tone at controlled volume.
Make the account exact, with pauses and ordinary breath resets.

body.text: Keep the torso with valued company despite attention pulling away.
Tighten and release the hands around a safely held prop.
Keep the base near the boundary you have chosen to preserve.

levels.label: Consuming
levels.felt_state: Hostility organizes choices and excludes competing interpretations of the target.
levels.face: The gaze becomes selective, fixing on evidence consistent with the settled judgment. Brows and mouth remain unusually still; a late blink or small cheek contraction marks the cost of hearing a favorable account of the target.
levels.voice: Keep a low, flat register or an impersonal ordinary one. Tone is unwelcoming and exact at chosen volume; slow categorical phrases, abbreviate conciliatory discussion, and let long pauses with comfortable breaths signal refusal to reopen the premise.
levels.body: Reorganize proximity, seating or participation to avoid affiliation. Arms become spare, hands refuse a symbolic exchange, and the whole base stays aligned with the chosen exclusion even when others attempt to draw the character closer.
levels.timing: A favorable fact is heard but fails to reorganize the established judgment.
levels.restrained_alternative: Maintain civil cooperation while making a firm private plan to end all optional involvement.
levels.recovery: New evidence must be taken seriously before the stance can soften; lower arousal alone is not reconciliation.
levels.playable_direction: Hold to the exclusion even when the room asks for accommodation.

face.text: Fix selectively on evidence that fits the established hostile judgment.
Let the brow remain unusually still during conciliatory discussion.
Keep the mouth controlled when hearing favorable claims about the target.

voice.text: Use low flat pitch or an impersonal ordinary register.
Make the tone unwelcoming and exact without compulsory growling.
Slow categorical phrases and leave long, comfortably breathed pauses.

body.text: Reorient the torso so affiliation is no longer physically offered.
Refuse the symbolic exchange while maintaining necessary practical control.
Keep the base aligned with exclusion despite invitations to approach.

levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: The hostile orientation saturates experience and threatens to organize everything around the target.
levels.face: Use a fixed look or a complete refusal to look, chosen clearly. Forehead and mouth may become blank, then a small lip tremor breaks through when the target is named; the head remains deliberately turned away.
levels.voice: A sparse, low statement or silence can carry overwhelming hostility. Keep tone cold or emptied, volume independent of intensity; use minimal contour, slowed isolated phrases, and long naturally breathed pauses rather than compulsory threats, snarling or sustained shouting.
levels.body: Choose a final withdrawal, rooted refusal or formal separation. Set shared objects down, open the hands, and turn torso and base toward the chosen life outside the encounter; avoid making physical attack the inevitable culmination.
levels.timing: The peak may be the recognition that continued contact consumes every other priority.
levels.restrained_alternative: End participation at normal volume, with a precise boundary and no theatrical farewell.
levels.recovery: Recovery can begin with restored attention to other people and goals; forgiveness is a separate possible process.
levels.playable_direction: Choose whether the target will keep owning your attention.

face.text: Choose a fixed look or a complete refusal of eye contact.
Allow the forehead to become nearly blank beneath consuming hostility.
Let one small lip movement break the stillness when named.

voice.text: Use sparse low pitch with minimal contour and precise endings.
Keep the tone cold or emptied at any comfortable volume.
Leave long naturally breathed pauses instead of supplying compulsory threats.

body.text: Turn the torso toward a chosen life outside the encounter.
Set shared objects down and let the hands open.
Commit the base to separation through a deliberate final movement.

variants.label: Hostility toward a known person
variants.context: A history of injury has made a once-known person an enduring hostile target.
variants.objective: Maintain separation despite familiarity and appeals to shared history.
variants.face_modifier: Let familiar details register without allowing the former warmth to complete.
variants.voice_modifier: Contrast exact present boundaries with any remembered cadence of closeness.
variants.body_modifier: Interrupt habitual gestures of intimacy before they reach completion.
variants.timing_modifier: Use reminders of history to complicate, rather than erase, the hostility.

seven_levels.modifier: Catch an old welcoming reflex and let it stop before becoming a full gesture.
Answer necessary business while declining the familiar form of address or easy private joke.
State what contact is permitted and let a shared-memory appeal meet a measured pause.
After a repeated boundary crossing, remove the familiar privilege explicitly and without unnecessary explanation.
Let recognition of the person’s old manner briefly disturb the face, then recommit to distance.
Refuse to let shared history substitute for present accountability, even when others invite reconciliation.
End the encounter or formalize separation; the peak can contain grief for the relationship without restoring access.

variants.label: Hostility toward a represented target
variants.context: An institution, cause or distant person embodies something the character experiences as fundamentally harmful.
variants.objective: Prevent endorsement or influence in the immediate scene.
variants.face_modifier: Focus on the symbol, document or representation that makes the target present.
variants.voice_modifier: Ground opposition in the character’s concrete stakes rather than generic villainous denunciation.
variants.body_modifier: Use refusal of participation, a signature or a displayed token as the practical action.
variants.timing_modifier: Make abstract hostility visible through a specific choice available now.

seven_levels.modifier: Notice the symbol and lose a trace of warmth while continuing the immediate task.
Decline an optional association and give a short reason if the situation calls for one.
Name why the representation is unwelcome here and ask for a concrete change.
Refuse a proposed endorsement, turning the document or token back without performative destruction.
Let the target’s influence intrude on an otherwise unrelated decision and consciously inspect that interference.
Organize a clear practical opposition while keeping allies, constraints and consequences within view.
Stop an act of participation or leave the setting; total felt opposition does not require dehumanizing language or violent action.

temporal_arc.onset: A target is interpreted through a history or category of enduring harm.
temporal_arc.escalation: Reminders and new evidence reinforce the hostile orientation and extend its reach.
temporal_arc.apex: Exclusion, opposition or total refusal makes the stance consequential.
temporal_arc.recovery: Separation may reduce activation; changed appraisal is needed to alter the underlying attitude.
temporal_arc.carryover: Hostility can persist through calm scenes and be reactivated by names, symbols or contact.

transitions.trigger: The target commits a fresh intolerable violation in the present.
transitions.bridge: Longstanding coldness abruptly narrows into an urgent demand and arrested action.

transitions.trigger: The character recognizes what the hostile relationship has cost or destroyed.
transitions.bridge: Let attention leave the target and land on the absent life or bond beneath the opposition.

transitions.trigger: The character begins relinquishing the claim while maintaining chosen boundaries.
transitions.bridge: Allow one less guarded look and restore attention to other priorities without requiring renewed closeness.

prompt_example.spoken_text: I thought you would be here.
prompt_example.visual_direction: Withhold the habitual greeting, keep a deliberate distance, and meet the eyes only for the necessary exchange.
prompt_example.delivery_direction: Speak in a low, exact register; let the line identify a broken expectation without offering renewed intimacy.

cue_conflicts: Hate may be cool and functional; rage-like arousal is an optional blend.
Avoidance and active opposition are different objectives and should not be ordered simultaneously.
A global hostile appraisal does not establish that its target is objectively harmful.
emotions.context_notes: Build hostility from character history and actual stakes, never from demographic coding. Cultural rules and power shape how separation is expressed. Use accessible equivalents for leaving or blocking affiliation, including gaze, timing and refusal of a symbolic exchange.

emotions.label: Disgust
emotions.definition: An aversive rejection of something experienced as offensive to contact, intake or closeness; sensory and moral contexts can recruit different expressions without sharing a mandatory facial signature.
emotions.appraisal: I do not want this in contact with me, inside me or in the space I am accepting.
emotions.objective: Stop contact or intake and establish a tolerable distance.
action_tendencies: Check what has already been touched
distinctions: Fear anticipates harm; disgust can reject something judged safe but offensive.
Revulsion emphasizes a sharper recoil or repelled reaction.
Contempt devalues standing; disgust emphasizes aversive contact or acceptance.

face.brows_forehead: Brows can lower at the source or lift with first detection.
face.eyelids: Lids narrow during inspection or close briefly to interrupt exposure.
face.gaze: Look at the offending detail, then toward a clean or tolerable alternative.
face.blink: Blinking can accompany a turn away from exposure.
face.cheeks: Upper cheeks may lift as the nose and upper lip gather.
face.nose_nostrils: An optional nose wrinkle can be localized and brief.
face.lips_mouth: Upper lip may lift, lips seal or mouth corners pull down.
face.jaw_chin: Chin retracts and jaw may open slightly before closing against intake.
face.head_neck: Head withdraws or turns away while eyes verify distance.
face.complexion: No automatic pallor or flushing; baseline and scene conditions govern appearance.

voice.pitch_register: A brief upward register at detection can settle into a lower rejecting line.
voice.pitch_range_contour: Use a recoiling rise followed by a compact downward refusal.
voice.loudness: Often quiet and close; volume depends on whether others need warning.
voice.tempo_rhythm: An interrupted word or delayed restart can reflect avoiding another intake.
voice.stress: Stress the source, contact or refusal rather than all words equally.
voice.articulation: Speech may become careful if the character is avoiding contact near the mouth.
voice.resonance: A drier or less open sound can be chosen without constriction.
voice.texture: Tone may be sour, incredulous or fastidiously neutral.
voice.breath_phrasing: Use comfortable breaths after turning away; never require prolonged breath holding.
voice.pauses: Pause before naming the source or deciding how to remove it.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A small “ugh,” exhale or involuntary-sounding catch is optional and safely voiced.

body.head_neck: Head withdraws before the whole body necessarily moves.
body.shoulders: Shoulders may draw back to increase the contact margin.
body.chest_torso: Torso angles away from the source while remaining able to inspect it.
body.arms_elbows: Elbows pull inward or extend an object away from the chest.
body.hands_fingers: Fingers minimize contact or release an object safely onto a surface.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight shifts away from exposure toward a tolerable base.
body.legs_feet: Feet reorient toward clearer space without compulsory stumbling.
body.gait: A short practical retreat can establish enough distance to act.
body.proxemics: Choose a meaningful margin from the specific offending source.
body.touch_props: Use a tissue, utensil or barrier only if available and plausible.
body.stillness: Stillness can preserve a no-contact boundary while another person removes the source.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: A small sensory mismatch makes contact less welcome.
levels.face: The eyes inspect the detail and the nose gathers briefly without a full grimace. One upper-lip edge lifts, then settles; the chin draws back only enough to interrupt an automatic approach.
levels.voice: Stay near habitual register with a tiny upward reaction and low falling assessment. Tone is mildly sour at normal or reduced volume; slow before the source word, pause to reconsider contact, and take an ordinary breath after looking away.
levels.body: Stop the hand just short of contact. Let the torso pull back a fraction while the base stays stable, then change grip or use an available tool; keep the rest of the body unremarkable.
levels.timing: The reaction follows detection and can vanish when the detail proves harmless or acceptable.
levels.restrained_alternative: Leave the face neutral and quietly choose a different point of contact.
levels.recovery: A benign explanation or removal restores the original action quickly.
levels.playable_direction: Check the detail before letting it close the distance.

face.text: Inspect the offending detail before choosing a tolerable alternative.
Gather the nose briefly without expanding into a full grimace.
Lift one upper-lip edge, then settle the mouth again.

voice.text: Use a tiny upward reaction followed by a low assessment.
Keep the tone mildly sour at ordinary or reduced volume.
Slow before naming the source and breathe after looking away.

body.text: Pull the torso back a fraction while preserving useful access.
Stop the hand short of contact and revise the grip.
Keep weight stable while deciding whether contact is still acceptable.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: The source is unpleasant enough to avoid voluntarily.
levels.face: A localized nose wrinkle lifts the upper cheek; gaze checks the source and then the exit from contact. Lips close firmly for a beat, and the head angles away while the eyes finish inspecting.
levels.voice: Use a small higher onset followed by a lower refusal. Tone is dry or fastidious, volume modest; give a short explanation, leave a pause before another look, and breathe comfortably in the turned-away position before finishing the phrase.
levels.body: Draw the object away from the chest or move the hand back. Shift the torso and weight toward clearer space, keep elbows economical, and set the object down carefully rather than flinging it.
levels.timing: Let the practical removal follow the first completed appraisal.
levels.restrained_alternative: Maintain polite features while declining the item with a precise hand movement.
levels.recovery: Distance permits facial release, though a checking glance may remain.
levels.playable_direction: Create enough separation to make an ordinary choice again.

face.text: Check the source, then look toward a route out of contact.
Localize the nose wrinkle to the newly noticed unpleasant property.
Close the lips firmly before a polite, precise refusal.

voice.text: Start slightly higher and fall into a lower rejecting line.
Use a dry fastidious tone at a modest volume.
Pause before another look and breathe comfortably while turned away.

body.text: Shift the torso toward clearer space without a startled full recoil.
Draw the object away and set it down carefully.
Transfer weight only enough to establish a tolerable contact margin.

levels.label: Clear
levels.felt_state: A clear rejection interrupts the intended interaction or intake.
levels.face: Wrinkle the nose or lift the upper lip briefly as the eyes narrow on the source. The mouth then seals, cheeks remain raised, and the chin retracts before gaze moves toward a tolerable alternative.
levels.voice: Begin with a brief safely voiced aversive sound or interrupted word, then settle into a low, falling refusal. Tone is sour but unforced, volume conversational; pace slows around the source, pauses allow removal, and ordinary breath resumes away from exposure.
levels.body: Pull the torso back while an arm extends the object to a safe resting place. Fingers release carefully, weight shifts away, and feet or chair angle establish a new contact boundary before discussion continues.
levels.timing: Make the rejection immediate, then give the practical decision its own slower beat.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the mouth closed and communicate the refusal through a small head turn and open stopping palm.
levels.recovery: Removing the source restores speech before willingness to approach returns.
levels.playable_direction: Refuse contact while still solving what happens to the source.

face.text: Look at the source, then deliberately choose a tolerable visual alternative.
Use one brief nose wrinkle rather than sustaining maximum contraction.
Seal the mouth after the short, clearly formed refusal.

voice.text: Let an interrupted onset settle into a low falling refusal.
Use a sour but unforced tone at conversational volume.
Slow around the source and allow ordinary breathing after removal.

body.text: Pull the torso back while preserving a stable handling position.
Extend the object to a safe resting place and release carefully.
Shift weight away to establish a clear new contact boundary.

levels.label: Strong
levels.felt_state: Continued exposure makes rejection harder to mask.
levels.face: The nose and upper cheek gather again when the source moves closer. Eyes narrow then turn away, lips pull down or seal, and the jaw loosens after the head has withdrawn enough to reduce exposure.
levels.voice: Use a higher, clipped interruption followed by a steadier lower instruction. Tone is openly aversive at firm comfortable volume; speak in short phrases, pause while the source is moved, and take normal breaths rather than maintaining a held intake.
levels.body: Lean or step away with a clear destination. Keep elbows near the body until a safe tool is available, turn the torso aside, and plant the base before attempting any cleanup or transfer.
levels.timing: Escalate when the source remains present or another person presses it closer.
levels.restrained_alternative: Use exceptionally neutral words while the body makes an unmistakable no-contact margin.
levels.recovery: Allow distance and a moment of ordinary breathing before reinspection.
levels.playable_direction: Get the source away without increasing your contact with it.

face.text: Turn the eyes away when the source moves closer again.
Gather the nose briefly at the renewed unwanted exposure.
Seal or lower the mouth corners as the head withdraws.

voice.text: Use a higher clipped interruption followed by a lower instruction.
Keep the aversive tone clear at firm comfortable volume.
Speak in short phrases with pauses for removal and breathing.

body.text: Lean or turn the torso away toward a tolerable destination.
Keep hands close until a safe handling method is available.
Plant the base before attempting any practical cleanup or transfer.

levels.label: Intense
levels.felt_state: The aversion dominates attention and interferes with necessary handling.
levels.face: Eyes repeatedly check the source despite attempts to look elsewhere. Brows knit above narrowed lids, upper lip lifts in a held fragment of rejection, and the chin stays drawn back while the mouth struggles to form a practical request.
levels.voice: Choose a thin, higher onset or a deliberately low controlled register. Tone is taut but easy, volume quiet to firm; shorten phrases to instructions, let pauses interrupt approach, and breathe normally after turning away before another attempt at speech.
levels.body: Begin a necessary reach, stop it, and recruit an available barrier or another method. The torso stays angled away, fingers remain spread from unwanted contact, and the pelvis holds the body in a stable retreat-ready position.
levels.timing: An aborted handling attempt shows intensity more specifically than a repeated full grimace.
levels.restrained_alternative: Remain still and ask for a tool or distance in a low exact voice.
levels.recovery: A reliable barrier or removal permits action; residual aversion may persist at the contact point.
levels.playable_direction: Find a way to deal with it that you can tolerate.

face.text: Recheck the source despite attempts to keep attention elsewhere.
Hold a small nasal gathering as a necessary approach becomes difficult.
Maintain a fragment of upper-lip rejection before forming the request.

voice.text: Choose a higher thin onset or deliberately low controlled register.
Let the tone feel taut without squeezing or forcing sound.
Use short instructions, approach pauses and ordinary breaths after turning away.

body.text: Angle the torso away while searching for a workable handling method.
Stop the reach and recruit a real barrier or alternate tool.
Ground the pelvis so withdrawal remains available without unstable movement.

levels.label: Consuming
levels.felt_state: The source occupies awareness even after immediate contact ends.
levels.face: The gaze returns to where contact occurred, then away in a rapid checking loop. Cheeks and nose gather in smaller repeated reactions; lips stay closed between sparse words, and the head maintains its withdrawn angle.
levels.voice: Use a narrow register with brief upward breaks when the source is mentioned. Tone is tight in feeling but unforced, volume often reduced; pace stalls around contact details, long pauses allow comfortable breath resets, and instructions remain short and specific.
levels.body: Keep the affected hand away from the body or hold the object at a safe distance until it can be placed. Torso and feet organize toward a practical cleanup or exit rather than aimless recoil.
levels.timing: The afterimage or remembered contact becomes a new trigger after the visible source is gone.
levels.restrained_alternative: Perform necessary steps methodically with a neutral face and minimal speech.
levels.recovery: Completion of a sensible cleanup and changed surroundings can let attention release gradually.
levels.playable_direction: Finish the practical separation your attention does not yet trust.

face.text: Return the eyes to the contact point, then look away again.
Allow small after-reactions instead of one continuously maximal nose wrinkle.
Keep the lips closed between sparse, practical handling instructions.

voice.text: Use narrow pitch with brief upward breaks at source reminders.
Keep the tone unforced even while the feeling remains taut.
Stall around contact details and reset comfortably through longer pauses.

body.text: Orient the torso toward a practical cleanup or exit route.
Keep the affected hand clear until sensible cleanup is possible.
Organize the base for practical separation instead of aimless recoil.

levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: Aversion overwhelms normal approach, speech or participation.
levels.face: Turn the face away or hold it still with eyes closed briefly, then reopen onto a safe point. Nose and upper lip may remain tense, but the mouth can become blank rather than sustaining a maximal grimace.
levels.voice: A sparse low refusal or a safely voiced broken phrase may replace ordinary speech. Tone thins, loudness remains a choice; pace becomes isolated words, pauses lengthen, and easy regular breathing stays available after exposure is reduced.
levels.body: Stop the attempted handling. Establish a stable supported position, keep hands clear of the source, and direct another person or choose a purposeful exit; the body’s main action becomes maintaining tolerable distance.
levels.timing: The peak may be a complete inability to take the next necessary approach step.
levels.restrained_alternative: Give a quiet final refusal while remaining immobile at the established boundary.
levels.recovery: Reduce exposure, restore ordinary orientation, then offer one manageable practical action if needed.
levels.playable_direction: Honor the limit long enough to regain useful action.

face.text: Reopen the eyes onto a tolerable point after reducing exposure.
Keep only the nasal tension that remains after turning away.
Let the mouth still rather than maintaining a maximal grimace.

voice.text: Use a sparse low refusal or a briefly unstable phrase.
Allow a thin easy tone at a freely chosen volume.
Use isolated words, long pauses and normal available breathing.

body.text: Stop the handling attempt and find a supported tolerable orientation.
Keep the hands clear while asking for a workable alternative.
Settle the base at a stable distance from the source.

variants.label: Sensory disgust
variants.context: Taste, smell, texture or visible material makes contact or intake aversive.
variants.objective: Stop exposure and handle the material in a tolerable way.
variants.face_modifier: Aim optional nose and upper-lip actions at a specific detected property.
variants.voice_modifier: Let the first response interrupt a taste, description or ordinary line without forcing gagging.
variants.body_modifier: Use actual distance, utensils or cleanup materials supplied by the scene.
variants.timing_modifier: Detection may precede conscious naming by one short beat.

seven_levels.modifier: Notice the unexpected property and inspect before completing the intended contact or intake.
Choose a different grip or quietly decline another taste, letting the practical choice reveal aversion.
Stop intake, set the source down safely, and form a clear refusal after an ordinary breath.
When exposure continues, turn away and request removal with short, useful instructions.
Attempt the necessary handling once, then use a barrier or alternate method when the body refuses direct contact.
Complete sensible cleanup while attention still returns to the remembered sensation; avoid endless ritualized repetition.
End exposure and stabilize before deciding what to do next; no forced gagging, retching or breath holding is required.

variants.label: Disgust at proposed complicity
variants.context: A proposal or act feels offensive to accept, endorse or be associated with.
variants.objective: Refuse participation and remove the implied association.
variants.face_modifier: Use a mouth closure or recoiling look; a literal nose wrinkle is optional.
variants.voice_modifier: Stress refusal of the act, keeping the moral claim distinct from contempt for a person.
variants.body_modifier: Set aside a document, payment or offered token that would signify participation.
variants.timing_modifier: Let the meaning of the offer register before rejection.

seven_levels.modifier: Let the offered implication alter the mouth before asking whether you understood correctly.
Decline the token or wording with a small head turn and a controlled falling line.
Set the proposal aside and state the specific part you will not accept.
After pressure continues, withdraw your hands or signature from the transaction and hold the refusal.
Let the prospect of being associated with the act interrupt fluent explanation; return to one exact boundary.
Remove your participation in practical terms while reminders of the proposal still pull attention back.
Leave or end the transaction quietly if necessary; overwhelming rejection does not require a literal contamination performance.

temporal_arc.onset: A sensory property or unacceptable association becomes salient.
temporal_arc.escalation: Closer contact, persistence or unavoidable handling increases the aversive response.
temporal_arc.apex: Refusal, recoil or stopped participation enforces a contact boundary.
temporal_arc.recovery: Removal, distance or a tolerable handling method restores useful action.
temporal_arc.carryover: Remembered sensation or association may briefly renew rejection after the source is gone.

transitions.trigger: The source becomes unexpectedly vivid or breaches the boundary.
transitions.bridge: A localized rejection spreads into a sharper head and torso recoil before words catch up.

transitions.trigger: The focus shifts from rejecting the act to devaluing its author.
transitions.bridge: Let the recoil subside into a cooler appraising look and reduced engagement.

transitions.trigger: The source is removed and no further contact is required.
transitions.bridge: Release the withdrawn head position, open the hands and let an ordinary exhale restore timing.

prompt_example.spoken_text: I thought you would be here.
prompt_example.visual_direction: Inspect the offered object, draw the chin back, and set it aside before looking at the person.
prompt_example.delivery_direction: Let the first word catch briefly, then deliver the line in a dry low register with a pause before “here.”

cue_conflicts: Localized nose movement and a neutral formal refusal are alternative displays.
Avoidance of smell does not require holding the breath; use normal breathing after turning away.
Sensory rejection and moral rejection can share an objective without identical facial choreography.
emotions.context_notes: Choose the source and degree of exposure concretely. Individual preferences, relationship, cultural food or etiquette norms, and power shape display. Adapt retreat to head angle, prop placement or gaze when movement is limited.

emotions.label: Revulsion
emotions.definition: A sharp repelled reaction to an intensely aversive encounter, often combining rejection, recoil and the urgent wish to end proximity; it can include disgust or horror without being identical to either.
emotions.appraisal: This is intolerably close or vivid; I need to break contact with it now.
emotions.objective: Interrupt exposure and regain enough distance or orientation to act.
action_tendencies: Seek a tolerable point of orientation
distinctions: Disgust can be a measured refusal; revulsion emphasizes an abrupt repelled reaction.
Horror involves appalling threat or violation and may hold attention despite recoil.
Loathing is sustained profound aversion rather than the immediate repelled beat.

face.brows_forehead: Brows can rise at impact, then contract during rejection.
face.eyelids: Eyes may widen before squeezing or narrowing away from the source.
face.gaze: A first fixed look can break abruptly toward a safe point.
face.blink: A rapid blink or brief eye closure can interrupt vivid exposure.
face.cheeks: Upper cheeks can rise with a nose and upper-lip gathering.
face.nose_nostrils: A brief pronounced wrinkle is optional, not compulsory.
face.lips_mouth: Mouth may open in a caught reaction, then close against further exposure.
face.jaw_chin: Chin withdraws; jaw opens and resets after distance is created.
face.head_neck: Head recoils or turns sharply before the torso follows.
face.complexion: Optional color changes are not required or diagnostic.

voice.pitch_register: A startled higher register can fall into low, sparse refusal.
voice.pitch_range_contour: Contours may break at onset and narrow during recovery.
voice.loudness: A short exclamation can be followed by quiet; sustained loudness is optional.
voice.tempo_rhythm: Initial speech may be interrupted, then return in short practical units.
voice.stress: Stress the immediate stop or distance required.
voice.articulation: First articulation can fragment before practical words become clear.
voice.resonance: Allow an open startled sound, then ordinary supported placement.
voice.texture: Tone may be shocked, thin or starkly controlled without forced rasp.
voice.breath_phrasing: Resume comfortable breathing after the recoil; never prescribe prolonged suspension.
voice.pauses: A wordless orienting gap can precede naming what was seen or felt.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A safely voiced gasp-like onset, “no” or aversive exhale may occur.

body.head_neck: Head and neck lead the withdrawal, within comfortable range.
body.shoulders: Shoulders draw back or turn to protect the front of the body.
body.chest_torso: Torso recoils, rotates or stops abruptly before approaching.
body.arms_elbows: Arms retract or open to maintain distance without required flailing.
body.hands_fingers: Hands release safely or hover away from unwanted contact.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight moves toward stable support or away from the exposure.
body.legs_feet: Feet plant before any purposeful retreat; avoid compulsory loss of balance.
body.gait: A quick retreat can resolve into stillness at a tolerable distance.
body.proxemics: Create a clear separation rather than indefinite backward movement.
body.touch_props: Place the source safely if possible; avoid reflexively throwing props.
body.stillness: A stopped approach or rigid distance can carry the reaction after the first recoil.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: A brief repelled flash interrupts approach.
levels.face: The eyes widen for a moment before a quick blink. One upper cheek gathers, lips part and close, and the chin moves back just enough to stop the face from arriving where it was headed.
levels.voice: Use a small higher onset that settles quickly into the usual register. Tone briefly thins at low or ordinary volume; interrupt the first word, pause to orient, and resume at a measured pace after one comfortable breath.
levels.body: Arrest the reaching hand and pull the head back before the torso changes. Keep weight stable, let fingers open away from the source, then choose a revised approach or simple refusal.
levels.timing: The recoil is brief and linked to a newly noticed property or implication.
levels.restrained_alternative: Make the repelled beat an interrupted reach and delayed answer with almost no facial change.
levels.recovery: A corrected interpretation can restore the original action after a checking look.
levels.playable_direction: Stop contact at the instant it becomes unacceptable.

face.text: Widen the eyes briefly before a quick interrupted-exposure blink.
Let the brows react once to the newly aversive detail.
Part and close the lips as the approach is arrested.

voice.text: Use a small higher onset that settles into usual pitch.
Let the tone thin briefly at low or ordinary volume.
Interrupt the word, pause to orient and resume after breathing.

body.text: Pull the head back before committing the whole torso.
Stop the reaching hand and open the fingers from contact.
Keep weight stable while selecting a revised approach or refusal.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: The encounter produces a clear but manageable recoil.
levels.face: Brows lift and draw inward as the eyes leave the source. The mouth opens in a small caught reaction, upper lip rises briefly, and the chin stays withdrawn while gaze finds an acceptable alternative.
levels.voice: Start slightly above baseline with a broken upward contour, then fall into a short refusal. Tone is startled and dry, volume modest; slow after the onset, leave an orienting pause, and breathe normally before explaining what must change.
levels.body: Pull the hand and torso back together, then settle onto a stable base. Elbows fold toward the ribs, fingers avoid unnecessary contact, and one small repositioning establishes space without prolonged retreat.
levels.timing: Give the first recoil and the subsequent decision separate beats.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the torso still but turn the head away and decline in a low controlled voice.
levels.recovery: Enough distance permits the eyes to return for a brief practical assessment.
levels.playable_direction: Get clear enough to decide what you are looking at.

face.text: Let the eyes leave the source and find an acceptable alternative.
Lift and gather the brows around the newly understood encounter.
Open the mouth briefly, then close it against further exposure.

voice.text: Begin above baseline, then fall into a short practical refusal.
Use a startled dry tone at a modest comfortable volume.
Slow after the onset and leave an ordinarily breathed orienting gap.

body.text: Pull the torso back with the withdrawing hand, then settle.
Fold the hands toward the body without prolonged flailing.
Establish a stable base at the newly tolerable distance.

levels.label: Clear
levels.felt_state: The repelled reaction interrupts the whole exchange.
levels.face: Eyes widen at recognition, then narrow as the head turns away. Nose and upper cheek gather, lips separate for an unfinished word, and the jaw remains loose while the chin withdraws from the source.
levels.voice: A short higher exclamation can break into a lower practical phrase. Tone is shocked or sour at comfortable audible volume; initial pace jumps, then slows sharply, with a full orienting pause and easy breath before any second sentence.
levels.body: Recoil through the torso and plant the feet or seated base. Retract the arms, safely lower any object, and turn one side away; stop moving once sufficient distance exists so the reaction has a definite endpoint.
levels.timing: The first beat precedes the explanation; the second is an attempt to regain organization.
levels.restrained_alternative: Let one quick head turn be the only overt recoil, followed by quiet exact instructions.
levels.recovery: Ordinary breathing and a stable view allow the next useful action to begin.
levels.playable_direction: Break exposure before trying to describe it.

face.text: Widen at recognition, then narrow the eyes while turning away.
Gather the brows after the initial impact has registered.
Part the lips for an unfinished word before useful speech returns.

voice.text: Let a higher exclamation resolve into a lower practical phrase.
Use a shocked or sour tone with comfortable audible volume.
Jump briefly in pace, then pause fully and breathe easily.

body.text: Recoil through the torso and stop once enough distance exists.
Retract the arms and safely lower any held object.
Plant the standing or seated base before choosing further retreat.

levels.label: Strong
levels.felt_state: The source remains vivid enough to make renewed approach difficult.
levels.face: A return glance produces another small eye widening and upper-lip lift. Brows knit as the character tries to inspect; the gaze breaks away again, and the mouth closes firmly around the abandoned description.
levels.voice: Use an unstable higher start followed by a grounded low refusal. Tone is thin but safely supported, volume chosen for the scene; speak in short starts, pause when the image returns, and restore a normal breath before naming a practical need.
levels.body: Attempt a cautious turn or reach, then stop and reorganize. Keep the chest angled away, hands near the body, and pelvis grounded; use a tool, different sightline or another person’s help where the scene permits.
levels.timing: Each renewed exposure, not a generic ongoing tremor, triggers the next recoil beat.
levels.restrained_alternative: Stay still at the boundary and communicate with a low, evenly paced sentence.
levels.recovery: A changed angle or reduced exposure can make a limited reapproach possible.
levels.playable_direction: Find a way to act without taking the full impact again.

face.text: Return the gaze cautiously, then break it when exposure renews.
Knit the brows during the attempted practical inspection.
Close the mouth around a description that cannot yet continue.

voice.text: Use a higher unstable start followed by a grounded refusal.
Let the tone thin without pushing volume or breath pressure.
Use short starts, exposure pauses and normal breath before naming needs.

body.text: Attempt a small turn toward the source, then reorganize.
Keep the hands near the body until another method appears.
Ground the pelvis before trying a different angle or tool.

levels.label: Intense
levels.felt_state: The repelled response disrupts speech and practical handling.
levels.face: Eyes close briefly after an involuntary return to the source, then reopen on a fixed safe point. Cheeks lift, lips remain parted without the planned words, and the chin stays tucked away from exposure.
levels.voice: Let a sparse higher fragment settle into a very low or ordinary register. Tone can sound hollow or taut at restrained volume; pace stalls, words arrive after substantial gaps, and comfortable breath resets precede requests for distance or assistance.
levels.body: The hands stop between reaching and retracting, then lower deliberately. Brace against safe support if needed, turn the torso away, and let feet establish a stable retreat position rather than scatter into aimless motion.
levels.timing: Hold the gap where a useful action was expected to happen.
levels.restrained_alternative: Give one quiet instruction and keep the face turned away until the source is managed.
levels.recovery: Assistance or reduced exposure restores sequence before the aversive memory fades.
levels.playable_direction: Let someone or something make the next step tolerable.

face.text: Reopen the eyes on a safe point after a brief closure.
Maintain the brow tension while useful words temporarily fail.
Leave the lips parted before the practical request becomes available.

voice.text: Let a higher fragment settle into a low ordinary register.
Use a hollow or taut impression with comfortably restrained sound.
Slow into substantial gaps and breathe before requesting necessary assistance.

body.text: Turn the torso away and use safe support if useful.
Let suspended hands lower deliberately instead of repeating the approach.
Establish a stable retreat position rather than scattering into motion.

levels.label: Consuming
levels.felt_state: The encounter persists as an intrusive sensory or moral impression.
levels.face: Gaze stays off the source but snaps back at a reminder. The brow remains creased, upper lip and cheek gather in brief after-reactions, and the mouth goes blank between incomplete attempts to describe the experience.
levels.voice: Use narrow low phrases interrupted by brief register breaks when recalling the source. Tone is thinned or stark, volume often low; slow the pace, allow long wordless intervals, and keep breath ordinary instead of simulating continuing choking or gagging.
levels.body: Maintain a turned-away torso after distance has already been achieved. Hands hover apart from touched areas or rest open, the pelvis stays supported, and feet stop moving while attention struggles to leave the exposure behind.
levels.timing: A remembered detail can renew the reaction after the immediate source is removed.
levels.restrained_alternative: Carry on a necessary task with minimal speech while one late head withdrawal exposes the lingering impact.
levels.recovery: Reorient to the present room and one manageable task; renewed exposure may briefly reactivate the response.
levels.playable_direction: Separate what is still happening from what keeps returning.

face.text: Keep gaze off the source until a reminder pulls it back.
Hold the brow crease through smaller recurring after-reactions.
Let the mouth become blank between incomplete attempts to describe.

voice.text: Use narrow low phrases with brief breaks at remembered details.
Keep the tone thin or stark without simulated ongoing choking.
Allow long intervals and ordinary breathing between sparse recollections.

body.text: Maintain an oblique torso after physical distance has already been achieved.
Rest the hands open or apart from the unwanted contact.
Let the base remain supported while attention leaves the exposure slowly.

levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: The repelled impact overwhelms the capacity to reengage.
levels.face: A fixed off-source gaze or brief closed eyes can replace further grimacing. Brows hold tension, lips open without words, and a small chin movement reveals the continued refusal of contact while the rest of the face stills.
levels.voice: Silence or one safely voiced low refusal may be enough. Keep register narrow or momentarily unstable, tone thin and volume optional; isolated words, long pauses and normal breathing carry the limit without any demand for retching, screaming or sustained strain.
levels.body: Stop attempts to approach. Settle into secure support or make a purposeful exit, keep hands clear, and orient the torso toward a tolerable point; complete immobility can protect the achieved distance.
levels.timing: The peak is the absence of a feasible next approach, even after others expect recovery.
levels.restrained_alternative: State the inability to continue softly and let a clear spatial boundary carry the rest.
levels.recovery: End exposure, restore orientation and allow time before asking for a detailed account.
levels.playable_direction: Stay with the limit until the world becomes usable again.

face.text: Hold the eyes on a safe point instead of rechecking repeatedly.
Retain a little brow tension while the larger reaction stills.
Open the lips without requiring a new verbal response.

voice.text: Use one low refusal or a momentarily unstable narrow register.
Choose a thin easy tone with no required loudness.
Leave long pauses and breathe normally without forced gagging or shouting.

body.text: Stop reapproach and orient the torso toward tolerable surroundings.
Keep hands clear while choosing support or a purposeful exit.
Stay securely grounded until another useful action becomes possible.

variants.label: Unexpected aversive contact
variants.context: An unforeseen touch, texture, taste or close sensory encounter triggers recoil.
variants.objective: Break contact and establish what was encountered.
variants.face_modifier: Let the first facial change follow contact before deliberate interpretation.
variants.voice_modifier: Start with a brief interrupted sound, then recover useful words without forced gagging.
variants.body_modifier: Give the recoil a safe endpoint and put any object down deliberately.
variants.timing_modifier: Differentiate immediate recoil from the later practical assessment.

seven_levels.modifier: Stop the contact midway and inspect the unexpected property with one brief backward head movement.
Withdraw the touched hand or face and allow a short orienting pause before naming the problem.
Break contact clearly, lower the object safely, and ask for a practical way to separate from it.
A tentative second look renews the recoil; choose a tool or another angle before trying again.
Let a necessary handling attempt stall, then ask for help rather than forcing repeated exposure.
After removal, react briefly to the remembered sensation while completing sensible cleanup in an organized sequence.
End further contact and stabilize; the character need not perform gagging or loss of balance to convey overwhelming revulsion.

variants.label: Repelled by a disclosure
variants.context: New information makes a person, act or proposed involvement suddenly intolerable.
variants.objective: Break identification or participation and orient to the implications.
variants.face_modifier: Let recognition widen the eyes before the gaze breaks from the speaker.
variants.voice_modifier: A familiar conversational register can collapse into a low, sparse response.
variants.body_modifier: Stop the ongoing gesture of affiliation or agreement at the moment the meaning lands.
variants.timing_modifier: The recoil follows comprehension, which may lag behind the spoken words.

seven_levels.modifier: Understand the implication a beat late and interrupt a small gesture of agreement.
Look away briefly, then ask one clarifying question that hopes the implication was mistaken.
When confirmation arrives, withdraw the offered hand or token and leave a wordless gap before refusal.
Attempt to restate the disclosure, stop at its appalling element, and establish immediate distance from participation.
Let the old view of the speaker fail in the face; keep the practical boundary clearer than the explanation.
React to a remembered detail after the conversation moves on, showing that comprehension is still unfolding.
End the exchange or hold silence at a firm boundary; the repelled peak can remain physically quiet and morally specific.

temporal_arc.onset: Unexpected contact or comprehension produces an abrupt repelled beat.
temporal_arc.escalation: Continued exposure or renewed recognition repeatedly interrupts reorientation.
temporal_arc.apex: Recoil, stopped approach or complete refusal establishes the limit.
temporal_arc.recovery: Distance and practical support restore a sequence of usable actions.
temporal_arc.carryover: Sensory or conceptual reminders can trigger smaller after-reactions.

transitions.trigger: The encounter reveals an appalling violation or ongoing danger.
transitions.bridge: The turned-away gaze is drawn back to comprehend what must be faced.

transitions.trigger: The immediate recoil settles into enduring profound aversion.
transitions.bridge: Large movement subsides while distance and refusal become stable rather than reactive.

transitions.trigger: Attention shifts from the aversive scene to someone suffering within it.
transitions.bridge: Look toward the person’s need, soften the rejecting mouth and choose one tolerable helping action.

prompt_example.spoken_text: I thought you would be here.
prompt_example.visual_direction: Interrupt the approach, turn the face away, then find a stable point before returning a brief look.
prompt_example.delivery_direction: Let the first word break off, breathe comfortably, and finish the line quietly with a stark falling contour.

cue_conflicts: A quick recoil and a fixed quiet aftermath are separate beats, not competing continuous instructions.
The reaction need not include nausea, gagging or loss of balance.
Turning away can reject exposure while concern for an affected person remains available.
emotions.context_notes: Choose a specific contact or disclosure and the character’s personal associations. Relationship, power and cultural expectations shape masking. Scale recoil to safe mobility and framing; eye direction or an interrupted hand gesture can replace whole-body withdrawal.

emotions.label: Loathing
emotions.definition: A sustained, deeply felt aversion to a person, object, practice or association, in which even reminders can feel intolerable and continued proximity is strongly resisted.
emotions.appraisal: The very prospect of closeness or association with this is profoundly unwelcome.
emotions.objective: Keep the target outside intimate, bodily or moral space and end unwanted association.
action_tendencies: Remove a target’s presence from personal space
distinctions: Disgust can be immediate and object-specific; loathing persists as a broader aversive orientation.
Revulsion is the sharper repelled encounter; loathing can be still, anticipatory and enduring.
Hate may organize opposition to a harmful target; loathing emphasizes profound unwillingness to be near or associated.

face.brows_forehead: Brows hold a small settled crease at the target’s appearance.
face.eyelids: Lids narrow or lower during an unwelcome recognition.
face.gaze: A brief appraisal can be followed by prolonged deliberate avoidance.
face.blink: A slow blink can interrupt acknowledgment before the head turns away.
face.cheeks: Cheeks tighten without requiring a repeated disgust grimace.
face.nose_nostrils: Nose movement can be minimal; a brief wrinkle belongs to selected reminders.
face.lips_mouth: Lips close against participation or draw into a small rejecting line.
face.jaw_chin: Chin retracts or angles away while the jaw releases between words.
face.head_neck: Head maintains an oblique orientation to reduce closeness.
face.complexion: No fixed color cue belongs to the state.

voice.pitch_register: A low or ordinary register can carry durable refusal.
voice.pitch_range_contour: Contours become narrow and final when association is proposed.
voice.loudness: Quiet is compatible with profound aversion; projection serves practical distance.
voice.tempo_rhythm: Measured refusal may replace an eager or socially fluent baseline.
voice.stress: Stress the boundary or unwanted association rather than a compulsory insult.
voice.articulation: Keep diction exact, especially when formal civility masks aversion.
voice.resonance: A dry, less inviting sound can mark the target-specific change.
voice.texture: Tone may be cold, sour or weary without vocal forcing.
voice.breath_phrasing: Use comfortable phrases with a reset before speaking the target’s name.
voice.pauses: A pause can precede touching, naming or accepting anything associated.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A low aversive exhale is optional; avoid continuous snorting or gagging.

body.head_neck: Head stays angled away even during necessary business.
body.shoulders: Shoulders and chest preserve a margin from the source.
body.chest_torso: Torso participates minimally and returns quickly to a tolerable orientation.
body.arms_elbows: Elbows protect personal space or keep an offered object away.
body.hands_fingers: Hands refuse optional contact and use deliberate practical exchanges.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight remains aligned with escape or separation.
body.legs_feet: Feet keep a route open and do not drift into intimacy.
body.gait: Movement may be economical and planned around avoiding the target.
body.proxemics: Choose a stable no-contact or no-association boundary.
body.touch_props: Set aside tokens of affiliation without requiring destructive handling.
body.stillness: Stillness can show an already settled refusal, not indecision.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: A reminder brings a faint return of established aversion.
levels.face: Gaze registers the target and lowers or moves aside. The lips close a little more firmly, one cheek tightens, and the chin angles away before any overt expression of distaste develops.
levels.voice: Stay near habitual register with a reduced contour on the reference. Tone dries at ordinary volume; delay the target’s name, keep the reply brief, and use an easy breath to return to the less aversive part of the conversation.
levels.body: Skip an optional touch or approach. Keep the torso on the existing task, hands within personal space, and weight unchanged; the target is quietly omitted from the body’s ordinary accommodation.
levels.timing: The reaction is a return of something known, not necessarily a fresh discovery.
levels.restrained_alternative: Give a neutral answer while choosing a more distant place for the associated object.
levels.recovery: The reminder passes when attention moves elsewhere; the orientation remains available.
levels.playable_direction: Keep the association from coming any closer.

face.text: Register the reminder and move the gaze aside deliberately.
Let a small brow crease acknowledge the known aversion.
Close the lips more firmly before continuing ordinary business.

voice.text: Keep habitual pitch with reduced contour on the unwanted reference.
Let the tone dry while preserving ordinary conversational volume.
Delay the name and breathe easily before changing focus.

body.text: Keep the torso on the task rather than offering approach.
Omit an optional touch or welcoming movement toward the target.
Leave the base unchanged instead of accommodating unwanted closeness.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: Anticipated contact is unwelcome enough to arrange distance.
levels.face: Lower the lids at the proposal, then look toward a practical alternative. The mouth forms a small rejecting line, nose movement remains optional, and the head turns before the torso follows.
levels.voice: Use a low-middle register and a compact falling refusal. Tone is cool or faintly sour at modest volume; speak measuredly, stress the contact being declined, and leave a short pause with a comfortable breath before offering an alternative.
levels.body: Reposition a chair, object or body angle to preserve distance. Keep elbows close, hands out of the offered contact, and pelvis oriented toward a tolerable route; the adjustment is deliberate rather than startled.
levels.timing: Prepare the distance before the source reaches intimate space.
levels.restrained_alternative: Offer a practical alternative in polite language while making the original option unavailable.
levels.recovery: Reliable distance restores function without requiring warmth toward the target.
levels.playable_direction: Arrange the scene so contact is unnecessary.

face.text: Look from the proposed contact toward a practical alternative.
Hold the brows lightly gathered while assessing unwanted proximity.
Form a small rejecting line before making the refusal.

voice.text: Use low-middle pitch with a compact and complete falling ending.
Choose a cool or faintly sour tone at modest volume.
Speak measuredly and leave a short pause before the alternative.

body.text: Reangle the torso to make the contact margin sustainable.
Keep the hands outside the proposed touch or handoff.
Reposition the base before the source enters intimate space.

levels.label: Clear
levels.felt_state: The aversion clearly governs choices about proximity or affiliation.
levels.face: Give the target a brief narrowed look, then withdraw the gaze. Brows hold a small crease, lips press before each necessary reply, and the chin stays angled away despite the target’s invitation to engage.
levels.voice: Keep a grounded register with narrow, final contours. Tone is dry and controlled, volume conversational; shorten explanations, slow the boundary phrase, and pause before any required name or acknowledgment, taking ordinary breaths without simulating contamination.
levels.body: Face the exchange only as much as necessary. Place the associated object aside, keep hands clear of optional touch, and settle the base at a deliberate distance that can be maintained without repeated retreat.
levels.timing: The refusal persists after the target becomes friendly or the object becomes familiar.
levels.restrained_alternative: Maintain formal courtesy while removing every optional sign of affiliation.
levels.recovery: End of contact releases immediate tension; the aversion need not be argued away.
levels.playable_direction: Make the no-contact preference clear and durable.

face.text: Give one narrowed appraisal, then deliberately withdraw the gaze.
Maintain a small brow crease beneath the formal courtesy.
Press the lips before each necessary, bounded practical reply.

voice.text: Use grounded pitch with narrow and clearly final contours.
Keep the tone dry and controlled at conversational volume.
Shorten explanations and breathe through pauses before required acknowledgment.

body.text: Face the exchange only as much as necessary business requires.
Place the associated object aside and decline optional contact.
Settle at a deliberate distance that does not require repeated retreat.

levels.label: Strong
levels.felt_state: Pressure to accept the target makes the aversion more active.
levels.face: A fresh approach prompts a brief nose or upper-lip gathering before the face stills again. Eyes move away decisively, cheek tension stays, and the mouth reforms a refusal after an attempted socially acceptable response.
levels.voice: Begin with a slightly higher interruption, then return to a low firm line. Tone is openly aversive but unforced, volume controlled; quicken the stop, slow the condition, and leave a long pause with an easy breath rather than repeated justification.
levels.body: Withdraw the offered hand or move the object back across the boundary. Turn the torso partly away, let weight commit to distance, and keep feet or chair aligned with a route that ends the pressure.
levels.timing: Escalation follows a boundary being pressed, not merely the target existing nearby.
levels.restrained_alternative: State the condition in formal terms while the body quietly makes further contact impossible.
levels.recovery: Respected distance allows practical attention to return; persuasion may prolong the aversion.
levels.playable_direction: Stop the attempt to make closeness feel obligatory.

face.text: Move the eyes away decisively when closeness is pressed.
Gather the brow briefly before returning to controlled stillness.
Let upper-lip rejection appear once before reforming the refusal.

voice.text: Start slightly higher, then return to a low firm register.
Use an openly aversive but unforced tone at controlled volume.
Quicken the stop, slow the condition and leave a long pause.

body.text: Turn the torso partly away to make further pressure impractical.
Withdraw the offered hand or return the object across the boundary.
Commit weight to distance while preserving a clear route away.

levels.label: Intense
levels.felt_state: Even indirect association becomes difficult to tolerate.
levels.face: Gaze catches on a reminder and immediately breaks away. The brow tightens, lips remain compressed around an almost-spoken rejection, and the jaw resets before the character can return to the current person rather than the absent target.
levels.voice: Use a narrow lower register with a small unstable rise at the reminder. Tone is sour or weary at chosen volume; pace slows around associated details, pauses interrupt otherwise ordinary conversation, and comfortable breaths separate the memory from the next practical sentence.
levels.body: Move the reminder out of personal working space or turn it facedown. Arms return close to the body, the chest reorients toward something tolerable, and the base stays stable rather than repeating a full recoil.
levels.timing: An indirect cue, such as a name or familiar object, now triggers a contact-like response.
levels.restrained_alternative: Remain outwardly composed and quietly request that the topic or object leave the immediate space.
levels.recovery: Changed surroundings and restored choice can reduce preoccupation without changing the underlying appraisal.
levels.playable_direction: Prevent the reminder from occupying the whole room.

face.text: Catch the reminder with the eyes and immediately look away.
Tighten the brow when indirect association intrudes into the present.
Compress the lips around a rejection you nearly speak.

voice.text: Use narrow lower pitch with a small break at the reminder.
Choose a sour or weary tone at a workable volume.
Slow around associated details and breathe before returning to present business.

body.text: Reorient the chest toward a tolerable person or activity.
Move the reminder out of personal space with one deliberate action.
Keep the base stable instead of performing another full recoil.

levels.label: Consuming
levels.felt_state: Avoidance begins organizing the scene and constraining useful action.
levels.face: Eyes keep checking where the target might reappear, then settle on a safe point. Lids remain narrowed, lips barely shape necessary speech, and the head stays oblique long after the immediate source has moved away.
levels.voice: A low, almost level register can carry sparse logistics. Tone is drained or cold, volume often quiet; pace becomes exact, long pauses precede unwanted references, and short comfortable breath groups support the few sentences needed to preserve distance.
levels.body: Select routes, seating or tasks around the aversion. Hands avoid associated props, torso turns are economical, and pelvis and feet remain assigned to separation; show the practical cost when a useful action is delayed or abandoned.
levels.timing: Let the audience see a valued opportunity lost because proximity feels intolerable.
levels.restrained_alternative: Perform essential duties impersonally while declining every optional involvement.
levels.recovery: A tolerable alternative or deliberate reconsideration can restore some flexibility before aversion lessens.
levels.playable_direction: Notice what the distance is costing without giving it up yet.

face.text: Check where the target might reappear, then choose a safe focus.
Hold the brows settled around the costly avoidance pattern.
Shape only the necessary words with minimal mouth movement.

voice.text: Use low nearly level pitch for the sparse practical logistics.
Make the tone drained or cold at quiet comfortable volume.
Pause before references and use short, ordinary breath groups.

body.text: Orient the torso around the chosen no-association arrangement.
Avoid unnecessary handling of props tied to the unwanted target.
Assign the base to separation while showing its practical cost.

levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: The aversion saturates the possibility of participation or closeness.
levels.face: Hold a nearly still face turned from the target, with a fixed off-source gaze. The brow may relax into blankness while lips remain sealed; one small upper-lip movement reveals the feeling when association is pressed again.
levels.voice: Silence or a low final refusal can carry the peak. Keep tone stark and unforced, register narrow and loudness optional; isolated phrases, deliberate pace, long pauses and normal breathing express a limit beyond further explanation.
levels.body: End participation or remain rooted at the established boundary. Set shared tokens down, leave hands open and separate, and align torso and base with a chosen exit or tolerable focus; no repeated recoil is necessary.
levels.timing: The peak can be the failure of any incentive to make the next contact possible.
levels.restrained_alternative: State the final condition at normal volume and stop negotiating your own proximity.
levels.recovery: Restore agency and tolerable surroundings; deeper change requires a changed relationship to the target.
levels.playable_direction: Reach the point where staying feels like accepting what you cannot accept.

face.text: Hold the gaze off-source without repeatedly testing your own limit.
Let the brow become quieter as refusal becomes complete.
Keep the lips closed until one final condition is needed.

voice.text: Use a low final line with very little pitch movement.
Keep the tone stark and easy at any chosen volume.
Use isolated phrases, long pauses and normal available breathing.

body.text: End participation or remain rooted at the established boundary.
Set the shared token down and keep the hands separate.
Align the whole base with a chosen exit or tolerable focus.

variants.label: Loathing of proximity
variants.context: A specific person or presence evokes sustained profound aversion.
variants.objective: Keep contact formal, limited or absent.
variants.face_modifier: Let familiarity intensify the withdrawal of warmth rather than trigger a stock sneer.
variants.voice_modifier: Use the target’s name sparingly when it carries an aversive weight.
variants.body_modifier: Maintain a clear distance and interrupt habitual or expected touch.
variants.timing_modifier: Contrast necessary business with the immediate retreat from optional closeness.

seven_levels.modifier: Let the expected welcoming gesture fail to start while the practical exchange continues.
Choose a seat or angle that makes accidental closeness less likely without announcing the reason.
Decline optional contact clearly and offer only the acknowledgment necessary to complete the task.
When the person presses for familiarity, withdraw the hand or turn the torso and restate the limit.
Let a remembered manner or phrase briefly intrude after the person leaves, then redirect to the present company.
Reorganize participation around distance, revealing the cost when something valued becomes inaccessible.
End the encounter or preserve a complete formal boundary in silence; no threat or physical aggression is required.

variants.label: Loathing of association
variants.context: A practice, role or symbol feels profoundly incompatible with the character’s accepted life.
variants.objective: Refuse to belong to, endorse or carry the association.
variants.face_modifier: Focus aversion on the object or implication that represents membership or complicity.
variants.voice_modifier: Keep refusal specific to the proposed association rather than globally devaluing everyone nearby.
variants.body_modifier: Set aside the badge, document, uniform item or token if the scene provides one.
variants.timing_modifier: Let the concrete offer activate the larger meaning.

seven_levels.modifier: Notice the symbol and delay the otherwise automatic act of accepting or wearing it.
Choose a neutral alternative and give a brief, controlled explanation if needed.
Put the token aside and state that you will not carry the proposed association.
After social pressure, repeat the refusal with less explanation and a firmer physical separation from the object.
Let indirect reminders contaminate the immediate task, then deliberately restore attention to what you can still endorse.
Accept a meaningful inconvenience rather than participate, showing the refusal’s practical consequence.
Withdraw entirely from the offered role or act; the peak may be a quiet unsigned page or untouched token.

temporal_arc.onset: A known target or representation brings sustained aversion into the present.
temporal_arc.escalation: Pressure, reminders or unavoidable association make distance increasingly important.
temporal_arc.apex: Complete refusal or withdrawal protects a boundary of proximity or identity.
temporal_arc.recovery: Distance restores function, while flexible reengagement depends on changed appraisal or context.
temporal_arc.carryover: Reminders may reactivate the aversion even in otherwise calm scenes.

transitions.trigger: The target unexpectedly breaches close space.
transitions.bridge: The settled avoidance becomes an abrupt head and torso recoil before practical speech returns.

transitions.trigger: Aversion becomes an enduring project of opposing the target’s influence.
transitions.bridge: Turn from mere separation toward planning and a more direct appraisal of the target’s actions.

transitions.trigger: Avoidance has cost something the character values.
transitions.bridge: Look from the excluded target to the lost opportunity; the rejecting mouth softens into an unfinished reconsideration.

prompt_example.spoken_text: I thought you would be here.
prompt_example.visual_direction: Keep a formal distance, set the offered token aside, and turn the face back only for the necessary sentence.
prompt_example.delivery_direction: Use a low dry register with a long pause before “you,” then end without inviting further closeness.

cue_conflicts: Enduring quiet distance and acute recoil are distinct phases; choose rather than stack them.
Loathing can target association without literal fear of contamination.
The depth of aversion does not justify treating a person as less than human.
emotions.context_notes: Ground the aversion in personal history, values or sensory experience, not identity stereotypes. Power and cultural expectations can require formal contact despite strong feeling. Gaze, object placement and response timing can substitute for physical withdrawal.

emotions.label: Joy
emotions.definition: A pleasurable recognition that something personally meaningful is good, present or possible; the episode may be expansive, private, tearful or quietly sustaining.
emotions.appraisal: This matters to me, and right now I can welcome it without solving it.
emotions.objective: Let the good event become real, then decide whether to share it or keep it close.
action_tendencies: Approach or remain with the source of pleasure
Repeat or savor the meaningful moment
distinctions: Amusement is organized around something funny; joy needs no joke.
Relief requires a lifted threat or burden; joy need not follow adversity.
Elation suggests a more pervasive lifted state; joy may remain anchored in one event.

face.brows_forehead: Forehead can unfurl after recognition; brows need not rise together.
face.eyelids: Lower lids may gather under rising cheeks, or remain relaxed in private gladness.
face.gaze: Find the meaningful person or object, then share a brief look with a witness.
face.blink: A recognition blink may interrupt looking; ordinary blinking resumes while savoring.
face.cheeks: Cheeks may lift gradually before the mouth visibly changes.
face.nose_nostrils: Keep the nose easy; a small sniff belongs only to a tearful choice.
face.lips_mouth: Corners can lift unevenly, part into speech, or settle into a contained smile.
face.jaw_chin: Jaw releases for a pleased exhale; chin may briefly tuck around private feeling.
face.head_neck: Head may incline toward the source, then level for mutual recognition.
face.complexion: Warmth or tears are optional and depend on individual baseline, light and makeup.

voice.pitch_register: Comfortable register may sit a little above baseline, or remain warmly grounded.
voice.pitch_range_contour: Phrases can acquire a buoyant rise and an unhurried resolving fall.
voice.loudness: Choose conversational presence, contained softness or an occasion-appropriate burst.
voice.tempo_rhythm: Speech may start promptly, then slow to savor a significant word.
voice.stress: Give the good thing or the other person the main emphasis.
voice.articulation: Consonants may brighten while meaningful vowels gain a little room.
voice.resonance: Allow an open, comfortable ring without making every line sing-song.
voice.texture: Clear warmth may alternate with a laugh-edged or tear-edged grain.
voice.breath_phrasing: Use easy breath groups; let a pleased exhale separate recognition from explanation.
voice.pauses: Leave a receiving pause before trying to describe the feeling.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A chuckle, delighted breath or quiet hum can replace explanatory speech.

body.head_neck: Orient toward the source without requiring a lifted chin.
body.shoulders: Shoulders may settle away from guarded elevation.
body.chest_torso: Sternum can become available while ribs remain comfortably mobile.
body.arms_elbows: Elbows may unpin for an offer, greeting or small celebratory gesture.
body.hands_fingers: Fingers can uncurl, touch a keepsake or find an offered hand.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight may move forward to engage or settle deeply into present support.
body.legs_feet: Feet may turn toward the source; no stepping is necessary in a close-up.
body.gait: If moving, allow a lighter initiation rather than a compulsory bounce.
body.proxemics: Invite closeness according to the relationship and the other person’s response.
body.touch_props: Touch can be offered and received; props may become objects of savoring.
body.stillness: Stillness can hold the entire experience while only the eyes change.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: Something good registers before it becomes a declared feeling.
levels.face: The gaze catches on the meaningful detail. A corner of the mouth loosens, one cheek begins to lift, and the forehead sheds a little task-related tension without requiring a full smile.
levels.voice: Keep the habitual register and conversational volume. Give one word a small upward curve, with a clear, lightly warmed tone. Pace stays functional; a short receiving pause and easy exhale let pleasure enter without a performed laugh or added breathiness.
levels.body: Interrupt an unnecessary hand adjustment, orient the head a few degrees toward the source, and let weight stop drifting away. The chest stays ordinary; pleasure is visible in renewed availability rather than a celebratory pose.
levels.timing: Recognition lands between an ordinary action and its completion.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the mouth neutral and let the gaze return once.
levels.recovery: Resume the task with a little less friction and vigilance.
levels.playable_direction: Notice the detail you would like to see one more time.

face.text: Return once to the detail that has quietly pleased you.
Let one mouth corner loosen before a full smile arrives.
Release a little forehead tension after the good detail registers.

voice.text: Give one personally meaningful word a small upward curve.
Warm the ordinary tone without adding a performed laugh.
Leave a brief receiving pause before continuing the task.

body.text: Orient the head a few degrees toward the good detail.
Stop one unnecessary adjustment as pleasure enters your attention.
Let weight stop drifting away from the source of pleasure.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: The good thing feels welcome enough to acknowledge to another person.
levels.face: Let the lips form a modest smile after the eyes arrive. Cheeks gather without squeezing the lids shut; a brief brow release and small head incline invite the other person into the recognition.
levels.voice: Use a comfortably buoyant register, a gentle rise on the shared detail and a settled ending. Volume remains intimate or conversational; tone gains lightness. Speak at an easy pace, pausing for their response and breathing freely between compact phrases.
levels.body: Turn the upper torso toward the witness, release the elbows from the ribs and let one palm become visible. Weight stays supported; an offered lean can establish participation without demanding proximity or touch.
levels.timing: Let acknowledgment follow the discovery rather than precede it.
levels.restrained_alternative: Allow one smile to escape, then return to ordinary composure.
levels.recovery: The smile recedes while the orientation toward the person remains.
levels.playable_direction: Show them that you also noticed the good thing.

face.text: Meet the witness briefly, inviting shared recognition of the good thing.
Let the cheeks gather after the eyes find the person.
Allow a modest smile that can change with their response.

voice.text: Use a comfortably buoyant register within the character’s habitual range.
Slow slightly around the detail you want them to notice.
Leave enough room for the other person to acknowledge it.

body.text: Turn the upper torso toward the person sharing the moment.
Release the elbows enough for a small welcoming gesture.
Keep weight supported while offering a modest lean toward engagement.

levels.label: Clear
levels.felt_state: Pleasure becomes an unmistakable experience that wants company or duration.
