levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: The felt stillness is so complete that it exceeds the character’s usual experience of composure.
levels.face: Keep the gaze awake and capable of meeting a person directly. The forehead, cheeks and jaw can remain almost entirely at rest; lips part only when speech is useful, and ordinary blinking preserves a living face rather than an idealized serenity mask.
levels.voice: Speech may be unnecessary, but any line stays clear and safely within the familiar register. Use a simple meaningful contour, an unforced steady tone and whatever volume communication requires. Pace is chosen, pauses spacious and breathing ordinary; there is no crescendo, trance effect or mandatory whisper.
levels.body: Choose supported, responsive stillness or a sequence of exceptionally simple actions. Hands remain available, torso balanced and head oriented to actual contact; no pose is compulsory. Overwhelming here means the depth of felt calm, not lost awareness, physical collapse or inability to respond.
levels.timing: The apex is profound settled presence with continuing access to the scene.
levels.restrained_alternative: Use almost no visible change; let an unhurried precise response reveal the depth.
levels.recovery: Continue with ordinary life as the unusually deep feeling gradually becomes less foregrounded.
levels.playable_direction: Let nothing inside demand a performance while you remain fully able to answer.

emotions.label: Love
emotions.definition: A valued orientation toward another’s existence, well-being and continued connection, expressed here as a present episode of affection within a broader bond.
emotions.appraisal: You matter to me beyond what you can provide in this moment, and I want to remain in meaningful relation to you.
emotions.objective: Let the other person feel recognized while honoring their separate needs and choices.
action_tendencies: Attend to the person as an individual
Support their well-being without requiring immediate reward
distinctions: Romantic love foregrounds desired romantic reciprocity; love can be familial, friendly or otherwise nonromantic.
Tenderness foregrounds gentle handling of vulnerability; love need not involve fragility.
Adoration emphasizes affectionate exceptional valuing; love can include clear-eyed familiarity and ordinary imperfection.

face.head_neck: Head can incline toward the person while preserving comfortable personal distance.

voice.tempo_rhythm: Pace allows the person to answer; intimacy need not mean slow speech.
voice.stress: Stress their name, particular need or shared meaning rather than generic endearments.
voice.articulation: Articulation can be familiar, clear or softly rounded without becoming baby talk.
voice.resonance: Use comfortable close resonance or ordinary public speech when appropriate.
voice.texture: Tone may be warm, playful, sober or openly affected.
voice.breath_phrasing: Easy breath groups support listening and complete phrases.
voice.pauses: Leave space for the other person’s response and separate choice.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A familiar chuckle, hum or soft acknowledgment can carry shared history.

body.head_neck: Head follows the person’s meaning, not merely their physical movement.

body.chest_torso: Torso turns toward engagement without assuming full frontal proximity.
body.arms_elbows: Arms can offer assistance, welcome or simply rest while listening.
body.hands_fingers: Hands may make practical care gestures or offer contact without taking it.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight commits to staying or adjusts to give the other person space.
body.legs_feet: Feet can orient toward connection; a seated or still performance is complete.
body.gait: An approach should answer the person’s welcome rather than assume entitlement.
body.proxemics: Closeness is negotiated through attention and response, not a fixed distance.
body.touch_props: Touch is relationship-specific and consensual; useful help may communicate more than an embrace.
body.stillness: Patient stillness can show willingness to remain without demanding a response.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: A familiar person’s presence quietly matters more than the surrounding task.
levels.face: Let the gaze find the person before the mouth changes. Brows ease, one cheek begins a familiar smile and the jaw releases; the eyes return to their immediate need rather than lingering on an idealized image.
levels.voice: Use the ordinary relationship register with a small warm contour and clear, unforced texture. Keep volume conversational and pace natural. Give their name or key word gentle emphasis, pause to hear the response and breathe easily; affection appears through specificity rather than a special romantic voice.
levels.body: Turn the head and a little of the torso toward them, leaving the current task available. A hand may stop its unnecessary movement or make room on a surface; weight remains supported while attention becomes more personally committed.
levels.timing: Recognition arrives before any explicit statement of affection.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the smile absent and respond accurately to one small need.
levels.recovery: Resume the task while retaining awareness of the person.

levels.label: Mild

Leave a listening pause after the greeting, take an ordinary breath and let the next phrase answer them rather than extend a rehearsed affectionate display.
levels.body: Orient the torso more fully and make one practical welcoming gesture. Hands can clear a place, offer an object or rest openly; weight indicates willingness to stay, while arms and distance leave the other person room to accept or decline closeness.

levels.restrained_alternative: Keep gestures compact and let sustained accurate attention carry the bond.

levels.playable_direction: Let them feel seen as themselves, not as the role they play for you.

emotions.label: Adoration
emotions.definition: Affectionate valuing in which a person or cherished being feels especially precious, remarkable or captivating, with a tendency to dwell on their particular qualities.
emotions.appraisal: You feel extraordinarily precious to me, and I want to remain with the wonder of your particular existence.
emotions.objective: Cherish the person’s distinct qualities without turning them into an object or erasing their ordinary needs.
action_tendencies: Protect time and attention for the valued person
distinctions: Love can remain ordinary and clear-eyed; adoration foregrounds exceptional affectionate valuing.
Admiration evaluates an admirable quality or act; adoration includes a cherished personal attachment.
Tenderness centers gentle care of vulnerability; adoration can be directed toward confidence, skill or everyday presence.

voice.texture: Tone may be delighted, reverent, playful or quietly overwhelmed.
voice.breath_phrasing: Give appreciation comfortable breath groups and room for response.
voice.pauses: Pauses allow looking and receiving rather than endless praise.

body.proxemics: Give the person space to be ordinary rather than keeping them under a spotlight.

distinctions: Sexual desire centers wanting sexual experience; romance can be nonsexual.

emotions.label: Longing

levels.label: Strong
levels.felt_state: The gap repeatedly interrupts the character’s ability to stay with present activity.
levels.face: Let the gaze leave the task and return to the absent destination despite an effort to stay present. Brows gather, lips press around a withheld address and a remembered smile briefly flickers; the chin steadies when the current emptiness reasserts itself.

levels.label: Intense
levels.felt_state: The desired connection feels central enough that its absence becomes deeply affecting.
levels.face: Let the remembered warmth fade into a quieter, openly affected face. Lower lids may moisten, inner brows lift and lips part on a name or unsaid question; the gaze stays on a concrete anchor while the jaw releases the effort to pretend the gap is small.

levels.body: Let unrelated movement stop and weight settle into support. Hands may hold the reminder carefully or rest empty, torso oriented toward the missing connection and head slightly inclined; the still body carries a strong inward reach without a compulsory collapse or pursuit.
levels.timing: The character stops minimizing the importance of what is unavailable.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep eyes dry and let one deliberate pause acknowledge the full gap.
levels.recovery: Return to a real present anchor without requiring the longing to disappear.
levels.playable_direction: Admit how much you want the connection while remaining where you actually are.

levels.label: Consuming

levels.face: Keep the gaze lucid but repeatedly drawn to the absent destination. Brows soften after strain, mouth opens on an unfinished thought and the chin gathers briefly; a slow blink can mark returning to the room, without turning absorption into a vacant stare.

Pace is spacious, pauses expose the missing response and normal breaths keep the delivery grounded; words may stop when they cannot bridge the distance.
levels.body: Find stable support and let hands remain with one meaningful object or simply empty. The torso stays directed toward the reminder while the head occasionally returns to present contact; a halted approach may be enough, with no repeated pacing or escalating attempts to cross another person’s boundary.
levels.timing: Return to the present requires deliberate reorientation rather than a larger outward display.
levels.restrained_alternative: Use supported stillness and one quiet acknowledgment of what cannot be reached now.
levels.recovery: Complete a small present action or accept company without erasing the absent bond.
levels.playable_direction: Let the pull be enormous while choosing one thing that keeps you in the present.

levels.voice: Speech may reduce to one name or clear sentence in the safe familiar register. Use a simple reaching or falling contour and an unforced aching, warm or moist tone. Volume remains optional; leave long pauses, breathe comfortably and avoid forced sobbing or treating intensity as permission to pressure contact.
levels.body: Choose stable, supported stillness. Hands rest or hold an actual reminder, torso remains organized and weight secure; a small turn toward present support can be the only action. The unmet reach stays emotionally large without requiring pursuit, collapse or loss of awareness.
levels.timing: The apex is a sustained encounter with the gap, not necessarily an attempted crossing.
levels.restrained_alternative: Use ordinary posture and a single precise look toward what is missing.
levels.recovery: Reestablish orientation through present company or one manageable practical action.
levels.playable_direction: Let the absence be fully felt without making the unavailable connection responsible for ending it.

emotions.context_notes: Editorial options depend on what is absent, individual baseline, relationship, power and cultural meanings of separation. Use accessible reminders and movement; do not assume longing is romantic or that visible distance equals emotional distance.

emotions.label: Compassion
emotions.definition: Concern for another’s suffering together with an orientation toward supporting them or reducing the burden, while keeping their needs distinct from the observer’s own distress.
emotions.appraisal: You are suffering, it matters, and I want to respond in a way that actually helps you.
emotions.objective: Understand the need, offer workable support and preserve the person’s agency.
action_tendencies: Attend to suffering without turning away
Ask or infer what support is wanted from context
distinctions: Empathic pain foregrounds feeling another’s distress; compassion foregrounds concern and helpful response.
Sympathy acknowledges another’s hardship without requiring shared distress or an immediate action aim.
Tenderness is gentle handling and can occur without suffering.

face.eyelids: Lids stay attentive without compulsory tears or sorrowful narrowing.
face.gaze: Follow the person’s face, words and comfort rather than inspecting suffering as spectacle.

voice.pitch_range_contour: Contours acknowledge difficulty and resolve clearly on useful offers.
voice.loudness: Volume meets the listener’s needs and the environment.
voice.tempo_rhythm: Pace allows the person to finish and respond to an offer.
voice.stress: Stress the concrete burden, choice and available help.
voice.articulation: Articulation stays clear, avoiding vague soothing or automatic baby talk.
voice.resonance: Use easy resonance that can remain steady under strong feeling.
voice.texture: Tone may be warm, sober, firm or gently affected.
voice.breath_phrasing: Comfortable breath groups support listening and practical speech.
voice.pauses: Leave pauses for disclosure, consent and correction.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A brief acknowledgment may be more useful than repeated sympathetic sounds.

body.head_neck: Head tracks the speaker and useful evidence, not an imagined suffering tableau.
body.shoulders: Shoulders remain available rather than braced for rescuing.
body.chest_torso: Torso orients toward listening and practical action.
body.arms_elbows: Arms offer help without enclosing or taking over.
body.hands_fingers: Hands can prepare a useful object, remain still or offer consensual contact.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight becomes stable before assisting or staying beside the person.
body.legs_feet: Feet orient toward useful action when relevant; no mandatory approach.
body.gait: Movement follows the actual support task and the person’s preferences.
body.proxemics: Respect privacy and distance, including a request for space.
body.touch_props: Use props for concrete help; touch is not the default response.
body.stillness: Steady presence can be the useful action when no immediate solution exists.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: Another person’s difficulty begins to matter beyond the immediate transaction.
levels.face: Let the gaze stop treating the exchange as routine and attend to the person’s strain. Brows gather lightly, lips release a prepared reply and the chin inclines; the face registers concern without assuming the severity or meaning of what is seen.
levels.voice: Use the habitual register with a small acknowledging contour and a clear, sober tone. Volume stays appropriate. Slow the next question, leave room for an answer and breathe easily; avoid automatic reassurance before you understand what the person is actually dealing with.
levels.body: Pause the competing hand action and orient the head and torso more fully. Weight stays supported, arms remain available and distance need not change; the first compassionate act is granting attention before deciding whether practical intervention is wanted.
levels.timing: Concern interrupts a routine response before the character chooses an offer.

levels.label: Mild

emotions.label: Empathic pain
emotions.definition: An aversive emotional impact in the observer while witnessing or imagining another’s suffering; the observer feels affected by the suffering without literally possessing the other person’s experience.
emotions.appraisal: What is happening to you reaches me painfully, and I am struggling to stay with its impact.
emotions.objective: Remain oriented to the other person while bearing and regulating the distress their suffering evokes.
action_tendencies: Attend to or recoil from the suffering
Seek a way to reduce the painful impact
Move toward compassionate support when capacity permits
distinctions: Compassion foregrounds concern and useful response; empathic pain foregrounds the observer’s distress.
Sympathy can acknowledge hardship without sharing a strong painful feeling.
Physical pain is the character’s bodily pain; empathic pain need not reproduce the other person’s bodily movements.

face.brows_forehead: Brows may draw together or lift inward when the suffering lands.
face.eyelids: Lids can tighten, then reopen to remain with the person.
face.gaze: Gaze may alternate between the suffering and an ordinary grounding anchor.
face.blink: A blink can interrupt an overwhelming image or returning thought.
face.cheeks: Cheeks may tense with a held response or soften in affected concern.
face.nose_nostrils: Nose movement belongs to actual breathing or optional tears, not mandatory disgust.
face.lips_mouth: Lips may press, part on a withheld response or tremble slightly.
face.jaw_chin: Jaw can gather around distress, then release for a clear acknowledgment.
face.head_neck: Head may recoil a fraction or dip, then deliberately reorient.
face.complexion: Moist eyes or pallor are optional and non-diagnostic.

voice.pitch_register: Register may rise with impact or settle lower during deliberate composure.
voice.pitch_range_contour: Contours can break around difficult words and simplify during reorientation.
voice.loudness: Volume may shrink, stay ordinary or briefly rise; intensity is not loudness.
voice.tempo_rhythm: Pace can stall at painful information, then become intentionally measured.
voice.stress: Stress the concrete harm or the other person’s experience, not self-dramatization.
voice.articulation: Articulation may briefly falter before returning to clear speech.
voice.resonance: Use comfortable resonance; never force throat constriction to sound distressed.
voice.texture: Tone may be dry, thin, moist or lightly grainy within the safe habitual palette.
voice.breath_phrasing: Use manageable phrases with ordinary breaths; no forced breath catching.
voice.pauses: Pause when the impact interrupts comprehension or speech.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A small distressed exhale or soft acknowledgment is optional.

body.head_neck: Head may withdraw slightly, then turn back by choice.
body.shoulders: Shoulders can brace briefly as the suffering registers.
body.chest_torso: Torso may recoil or become still around the impact.
body.arms_elbows: Arms can gather close or pause an intended helpful action.
body.hands_fingers: Hands may press together, grip a support lightly or deliberately open.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight shifts toward support rather than compulsory collapse.
body.legs_feet: Feet may orient toward staying or a brief needed distance.
body.gait: Movement can stop when the account lands; no reenactment of the injury is required.
body.proxemics: Manage distance without making the suffering person responsible for the observer’s comfort.
body.touch_props: Use a neutral support or prop for grounding if present; touch requires welcome.
body.stillness: Stillness can show the effort to remain present with painful resonance.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: Another person’s pain produces a brief felt impact in the observer.
levels.face: Let the gaze catch on the difficult detail. Brows gather slightly, lips press before a response and the jaw pauses; a small blink or fraction of a head recoil marks being affected, followed by returning the eyes to the person.
levels.voice: Use the habitual register with a briefly interrupted contour and a sober, slightly dry tone. Volume stays conversational. Let one word arrive later than intended, pause to take in the fact and breathe easily; then recover clear articulation without imitating the other person’s pain sounds.
levels.body: Pause the current hand action and let the torso register a small withdrawal or stillness. Weight remains supported, elbows draw closer for a beat and then release; the body shows impact without reenacting an injury or making a dramatic claim of identical suffering.
levels.timing: The reaction lands immediately after a specific painful detail becomes understood.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the body steady and let a short speech delay carry the impact.
levels.recovery: Return attention to the person’s actual words and present condition.
levels.playable_direction: Let the difficult fact reach you before deciding what to say.

Use a sober slightly dry tone without copying pain sounds.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: The observer feels enough distress to need a small reset while listening.
levels.face: Let the inner brows lift or knit as the gaze stays on the person. Lips part and close around an unused response, lids tighten briefly and then reopen; the chin steadies after a small downward glance that helps the observer return.
levels.voice: Stay in a comfortable register with a small broken rise and a quieter falling acknowledgment. Tone may be dry or gently affected at appropriate volume. Pace slows, a pause permits an ordinary breath and the next words become clear; avoid automatic soothing that bypasses the painful fact.
levels.body: Gather the hands briefly or touch an available support, then let them ease. Torso stays oriented despite a small recoil, weight finds stability and the head returns to the speaker; the reset is modest enough that the suffering person need not manage it.
levels.timing: A short grounding beat separates the first impact from continued listening.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the face composed and use a single careful acknowledgment.
levels.recovery: Resume listening at a manageable pace without denying the impact.
levels.playable_direction: Stay with them after the first impulse to turn away.

Let the lids tighten briefly, then reopen for listening.
Part and close the lips around an unused response.

voice.text: Let a small broken rise settle into a clear acknowledgment.
Leave a short reset pause before continuing to listen.
Take an ordinary breath instead of manufacturing a distressed catch.

body.text: Gather the hands briefly, then let them ease again.
Find a little more stability in the support already available.
Return the head toward the speaker after the first impact.

levels.label: Clear
levels.felt_state: The suffering clearly evokes painful emotional resonance in the observer.
levels.face: Let brows gather and lower lids tighten while the mouth loses its prepared social shape. Gaze may briefly move to a neutral anchor, then return; the jaw releases for a truthful acknowledgment, with moist eyes optional rather than required proof of empathy.
levels.voice: Use the familiar register with shortened, uneven contours and a sober or lightly moist texture. Keep volume appropriate to the exchange. Speak more slowly around the painful detail, pause when needed and breathe comfortably; clear concise language prevents the observer’s distress from overtaking the person’s account.
levels.body: Stop unrelated activity and settle weight into reliable support. Hands may press together and then open, arms remain close and torso stays present despite an impulse to withdraw; a deliberate return of the head toward the person makes staying an active choice.
levels.timing: The impact is followed by a visible decision to remain engaged.
levels.restrained_alternative: Use stillness and a dry face while the voice briefly loses fluency.
levels.recovery: Find one accurate acknowledgment or concrete support question.
levels.playable_direction: Let yourself be affected without claiming you know exactly what they feel.

Pause before responding so the account remains the center.

body.text: Settle weight into reliable support after stopping unrelated activity.

levels.label: Strong
levels.felt_state: The observer’s distress competes with the capacity to keep listening or helping.
levels.face: Let the gaze break briefly when the difficult image or account lands, then return deliberately. Brows draw inward, lips press around a withheld reaction and the chin gathers; the eyes remain responsive, avoiding a fixed tragic expression that continues regardless of new information.
levels.voice: Use a comfortable register with interrupted contours that deliberately become simpler. Tone may thin or roughen lightly without forced strain; loudness can remain low or ordinary. Break speech into short intelligible phrases, pause for normal breaths and allow a truthful acknowledgment instead of attempting continuous reassurance.
levels.body: Let the torso recoil a little, then reorganize over support. Hands pause mid-help or grip an available surface lightly before releasing; arms and head return toward the person. The body shows that remaining present now requires effort, without copying the other person’s injury.
levels.timing: Withdrawal and chosen return become two distinct beats.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep outward movement minimal and let one interrupted phrase expose the conflict.
levels.recovery: Reduce competing demands and choose one manageable way to remain useful.
levels.playable_direction: Notice the urge to escape the feeling, then choose how you can stay present.

levels.label: Intense
levels.felt_state: The other person’s suffering lands with deep personal force.
levels.face: Allow lower lids to moisten or the mouth to tremble briefly while brows lift inward. Gaze finds a stable anchor, then reconnects with the person; the jaw releases after an effortful first word, and the face need not remain continuously contorted.
levels.voice: Use a grounded familiar register, simple contours and a lightly moist, dry or grainy tone. Volume may decrease. Speak selectively, leave long pauses and take ordinary breaths; if the voice catches naturally, stop and restart comfortably rather than forcing a sob or constricted sound.
levels.body: Seek stable support and let the hands stop unnecessary work. Torso can become still, arms close and weight settled; then make one deliberate orienting movement toward the person. The observer’s strong impact is visible, but contact or reassurance is not demanded from the sufferer.
levels.timing: A larger emotional wave is followed by deliberate reorientation to the actual scene.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep tears absent and use a long, lucid pause before the next accurate response.
levels.recovery: Name a simple present fact or useful action to regain orientation.
levels.playable_direction: Let the suffering affect you deeply while keeping its owner in view.

levels.label: Consuming
levels.felt_state: Vicarious distress absorbs attention and temporarily limits fluent response.
levels.face: The face may become still after the strongest reaction. Gaze rests on a neutral anchor before returning, brows remain softly gathered and lips part without words; a slow blink and released jaw mark the effort to stay available rather than a compulsory breakdown.
levels.voice: Use brief fragments in the safe habitual range, with flattened or gently falling contours and an unforced affected texture. Loudness remains optional. Pace is spacious, pauses allow orientation and breaths stay ordinary; speech can wait instead of forcing reassurance through escalating vocal distress.
levels.body: Stop the competing action and find a secure seat or stance if needed. Hands rest on available support, torso stays organized and head returns toward the person when ready; a small respectful distance adjustment can preserve capacity without abandoning the scene or asking to be consoled.
levels.timing: The main beat is regaining enough orientation to remain in relation.
levels.restrained_alternative: Use quiet supported stillness and one clear statement of continued presence.
levels.recovery: Return through a manageable support role or appropriate brief space.
levels.playable_direction: Make enough room for the impact that you can continue seeing the person, not only your reaction.

Use a slow blink to regain usable attention.

voice.text: Let brief fragments wait between spacious orienting pauses.
Keep the affected tone unforced and within the habitual palette.
Use ordinary breaths instead of speaking through escalating distress.

body.text: Find a secure seat or stance if the scene permits.
Rest the hands on available support while orientation returns.

levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: The observer’s felt distress exceeds immediate expressive and attentional capacity.
levels.face: Let the gaze seek one stable point while brows and mouth remain affected but not continuously animated. Tears or dry stillness are alternatives; the jaw releases, chin steadies and the eyes can return to the person in short, deliberate moments as orientation becomes possible.
levels.voice: Speech may stop or reduce to one truthful acknowledgment. Use a safe familiar register, a simple contour and an unforced dry, moist or thin tone at suitable volume. Leave ample pauses and normal breaths; do not manufacture choking, forced sobbing or a claim of identical pain.
levels.body: Choose reliable support and reduce activity to what can be done safely and respectfully. Hands rest, torso remains balanced and weight secure; a brief request for space or a simple continued presence are alternatives. The body need not collapse or reenact the observed suffering.
levels.timing: The apex is intense impact with a gradual return of usable attention.
levels.restrained_alternative: Remain almost still and communicate one clear, bounded statement when ready.
levels.recovery: Reorient to present facts and a sustainable way of supporting or stepping back.
levels.playable_direction: Let the impact be real without making the suffering person responsible for repairing you.

variants.voice_modifier: Keep acknowledgments brief so the person’s sounds and needs remain primary.
variants.body_modifier: Use stable support and only helpful, agreed movement.
variants.timing_modifier: The impact follows concrete present cues.

cue_conflicts: Empathic pain does not require literal mirroring of another person’s injury or facial movement.
The observer can feel strong distress while remaining useful, or may need a brief respectful reset.

emotions.context_notes: Editorial options depend on individual baseline, relationship, power, cultural expression and current capacity. Keep the observer’s experience distinct from the sufferer’s; use accessible support, comfortable breathing and no forced reenactment or diagnostic inference.

emotions.label: Sympathy
emotions.definition: Concerned acknowledgment of another person’s hardship or misfortune, with an orientation toward recognizing their experience; it need not involve sharing their distress or knowing how to help.
emotions.appraisal: What happened to you is difficult or unfair, and your experience deserves acknowledgment.
emotions.objective: Communicate that the hardship has been heard without claiming it as one’s own or imposing a response.
action_tendencies: Make room for the person’s account or preferred privacy
distinctions: Empathic pain centers the observer’s painful resonance; sympathy can remain emotionally steady.
Compassion foregrounds a wish to relieve suffering; sympathy may primarily witness and acknowledge it.
Pity can imply unequal regard in some contexts; sympathy here does not require condescension.

face.brows_forehead: Brows may draw gently inward at the difficult fact, then relax for listening.
face.eyelids: Lids remain attentive without mandatory narrowing or tears.
face.gaze: Meet the person or use culturally comfortable gaze while leaving room for privacy.
face.blink: An ordinary blink can mark receiving the news before replying.
face.cheeks: Cheeks often stay sober, with a small warmth if welcomed.
face.nose_nostrils: Nose remains neutral unless tears happen naturally.
face.lips_mouth: Lips may press briefly in acknowledgment, then release for a clear response.
face.jaw_chin: Jaw stays unforced; chin can make one small acknowledging dip.
face.head_neck: Head inclines to listen without a repetitive pitying tilt.
face.complexion: No complexion change is required or diagnostic.

voice.pitch_register: Use the natural register rather than a special condolence pitch.
voice.pitch_range_contour: Contours can acknowledge the difficulty and resolve without sounding dismissively final.
voice.loudness: Volume suits privacy, distance and the listener’s access needs.
voice.tempo_rhythm: Pace gives the difficult information room without becoming ceremonially slow.
voice.stress: Stress the person’s specific experience rather than generic sympathy formulas.
voice.articulation: Articulation remains clear, respectful and ordinary.
voice.resonance: Use easy resonance without a manufactured mournful depth.
voice.texture: Tone may be sober, warm, matter-of-fact or gently affected.
voice.breath_phrasing: Comfortable breath groups support concise acknowledgment.
voice.pauses: Pause after the acknowledgment so the person can speak or stay quiet.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A brief soft acknowledgment can help; repeated pitying noises may intrude.

body.head_neck: Head turns fully enough to show that the news was received.
body.shoulders: Shoulders can settle out of competing readiness.
body.chest_torso: Torso orients toward listening without crowding.
body.arms_elbows: Arms remain available rather than automatically reaching to comfort.
body.hands_fingers: Hands stop distracting activity or make one respectful offer.
body.pelvis_weight: Weight commits to staying for the response if welcome.
body.legs_feet: Feet can remain still or orient to give privacy.
body.gait: Any approach should answer the person’s comfort and the setting.
body.proxemics: Respect the chosen distance; acknowledgment need not become intimacy.
body.touch_props: Touch and props are optional, appropriate to the actual relationship.
body.stillness: Quiet stillness after speaking leaves ownership of the moment with the person.

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: The character registers that another person has had a difficult experience.
levels.face: Let the gaze return from the task to the person as the fact lands. Brows gather lightly, lips stop preparing the routine reply and the chin dips a fraction; keep the face receptive rather than immediately arranging a generalized sorrowful expression.
levels.voice: Use the habitual register with a modest acknowledging contour and a clear sober tone. Volume remains conversational. Slow the response enough to show the fact was heard, leave a short pause and breathe easily; choose ordinary specific words rather than a rehearsed condolence cadence.
levels.body: Pause the competing hand action and orient the head more fully. The torso remains supported, arms unforced and distance unchanged; the small interruption gives the person’s hardship room inside the encounter without assuming they want extended comfort or disclosure.
levels.timing: Acknowledgment follows understanding, before the conversation moves to another topic.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the face neutral and respond to the actual difficult fact.
levels.recovery: Let the person’s reply determine whether to stay with the subject.
levels.playable_direction: Show that their difficult news did not pass through the conversation unnoticed.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: Concern becomes personally present enough for a modest sympathetic response.

levels.body: Turn the torso a little toward them and let hands rest rather than distract. Weight indicates willingness to remain, arms stay open to use without reaching automatically and the head follows their response; a small space-making gesture may be more appropriate than touch.

levels.restrained_alternative: Use a plain sentence and attentive stillness instead of a visibly sad face.
levels.recovery: Follow their choice to elaborate, change subject or remain quiet.

levels.label: Clear
levels.felt_state: Sympathy is clearly communicated while the other person retains ownership of the experience.

Name the specific hardship, leave a real response pause and breathe comfortably; avoid claiming exact understanding or making the sentence chiefly about your own feelings.
levels.body: Set aside the competing task long enough to receive the answer. Hands remain still or offer a practical choice, torso oriented and weight stable; the body communicates availability without enclosing the person, insisting on proximity or turning acknowledgment into a rescue scene.
levels.timing: A specific acknowledgment is followed by space for the person’s actual response.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep movement minimal and make the wording accurate and respectful.
levels.recovery: Continue listening or return to routine in the way the person prefers.
levels.playable_direction: Let them know you recognize the hardship without deciding how they should feel about it.

levels.label: Strong

emotions.label: Gratitude
emotions.definition: A response to recognizing a valued benefit, care or effort as coming from another’s contribution or from circumstances the character does not experience as solely self-produced.
emotions.appraisal: Something that matters to me was given or made possible, and I want its source and significance to be recognized.
emotions.objective: Receive the benefit and acknowledge the contribution specifically without reducing it to a transaction.
action_tendencies: Turn attention from the benefit to its source
Carry the received care into future regard or action
distinctions: Relief centers a lifted burden; gratitude centers recognition of the contribution that helped.
Joy centers the good experience itself; gratitude adds acknowledgment of a source.
Indebtedness implies an obligation to repay; gratitude can exist without a debt claim or immediate reciprocity.

voice.pitch_register: Use the natural register; strong gratitude may become warmly grounded rather than high.
voice.pitch_range_contour: Contours can rise in recognition and settle into a sincere, complete acknowledgment.
voice.loudness: Volume follows audience and privacy, not the supposed size of the debt.
voice.tempo_rhythm: Pace slows for the specific contribution and leaves response space.

voice.resonance: Use comfortable resonant warmth without forced emotional projection.
voice.texture: Tone may be surprised, delighted, sober, dryly sincere or moist.
voice.breath_phrasing: Easy breath groups allow the benefit to be received before it is explained.
voice.pauses: Pause between noticing the result and recognizing the giver.
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A small laugh, pleased exhale or wordless acknowledgment may be sufficient.

body.proxemics: Closeness follows the relationship; gratitude does not create touch entitlement.

emotions.label: Fago
emotions.definition: A culturally lexicalized Ifaluk concept retained here with its relational specificity rather than reduced to an English synonym. This profile offers an explicitly editorial interpretation of affection, concern and sadness around a valued person’s vulnerability; its motor and vocal choices are not claims of authentic Ifaluk performance.
emotions.appraisal: Editorial scene appraisal: your vulnerability matters within our relationship, and affection makes the possibility or reality of suffering personally consequential.
emotions.objective: For this editorial interpretation, hold affection and sorrow together while responding to the particular relationship and the person’s actual needs.
action_tendencies: Attend to the vulnerability of a valued person
Maintain relational presence or offer appropriate care
distinctions: The approximate gloss “sad love” is explanatory and does not exhaust the culturally situated concept.
This editorial profile overlaps compassion and tenderness but does not claim that fago is their universal combination.
The selected variants are fictional relational situations, not documented Ifaluk subtypes or display rules.

levels.body: Stop unrelated movement and commit to one appropriate form of presence or care. Arms remain unforced, hands precise and torso balanced; weight stays grounded. A familiar practical gesture may be more meaningful than an added embrace, depending on what the scene establishes.
levels.timing: Shared history gives the vulnerable fact a second, more personal emotional wave.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the face composed and make one considerate choice that reflects the established bond.
levels.recovery: Let care return to ordinary action rather than sustain a tableau of sadness.
levels.playable_direction: Allow the relationship’s history to make this vulnerability personally consequential.

levels.label: Intense
levels.felt_state: Affectionate concern and sadness become deeply affecting without reducing the person to fragility.
levels.face: Let lower lids moisten or the mouth gather briefly while the gaze remains relational. Brows soften inward, cheeks retain a trace of familiar warmth and the jaw releases; the face can hold sadness and affection without claiming a unique configuration for the cultural term.
levels.voice: Use the character’s comfortable register, restrained personal contours and a warm or lightly moist tone. Volume follows access and privacy. Speak selectively, allow long listening pauses and easy breaths; avoid invented ceremonial cadence, forced sobbing or a vocal blend presented as an authentic Ifaluk signature.
levels.body: Find stable support and let hands perform only wanted care or rest. Torso remains available, head responsive and weight secure; the person’s competence and choice stay visible. Intensity can be expressed through careful presence rather than enclosing, rescuing or treating vulnerability as permanent helplessness.
levels.timing: A deeper emotional wave is followed by renewed attention to the person’s agency.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep tears absent and make the relational care precise and unshowy.
levels.recovery: Return to a concrete shared need or an ordinary moment of connection.
levels.playable_direction: Let sadness deepen the care without making vulnerability the whole person.

levels.label: Consuming
levels.felt_state: The mixed relational feeling fills attention and makes simple English labels feel inadequate.
levels.face: The face may become quiet, with a lucid gaze and a small affectionate smile that appears and fades. Brows remain softly concerned, lips part on an unfinished acknowledgment and the chin gathers; a blink gives the mixed feeling room without demanding tears.
levels.voice: Use brief phrases in the established register with gentle, sober contours and an unforced warm texture. Loudness stays situational. Pace becomes spacious, pauses hold what is difficult to summarize and breathing remains ordinary; this is a fictional performance interpretation, not a demonstration of a culture’s emotional expression.
levels.body: Stop unrelated tasks and choose a stable relational position. Hands rest or continue one careful agreed action, torso balanced and weight grounded; the head remains responsive to the person’s wishes. Supported stillness can contain the mixture without a culturally prescribed pose or required contact.
levels.timing: The feeling is sustained through presence after explanatory language becomes insufficient.
levels.restrained_alternative: Use one plain personal phrase and let the established relationship supply its meaning.
levels.recovery: Reenter ordinary shared life through a small care action or accepted silence.
levels.playable_direction: Stay with the person and the mixed feeling without needing to translate it into one simple emotion.

levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: Within the editorial interpretation, relational affection and sorrow exceed immediate expressive organization.
levels.face: Let the gaze remain clear and responsive while brow, mouth and jaw become very still. Tears, a faint familiar smile or dry composure are alternatives; the chin settles, preserving the person’s agency and avoiding any claim that this face reveals a uniquely Ifaluk feeling.
levels.voice: Words may wait or reduce to a truthful personal acknowledgment in the character’s natural register. Use a simple contour and unforced warm, sober or moist tone at needed volume. Leave long responsive pauses and normal breaths; no ritual, accent, vocal signature or culturally authentic intensity scale is implied.
levels.body: Choose grounded stillness or one carefully appropriate act within the established relationship. Hands and arms remain available, torso balanced and weight secure; contact follows welcome. The magnitude is held in relational attention, without assuming collapse, self-sacrifice, a traditional gesture or an obligation the scene has not established.
levels.timing: The apex is complete presence with the mixed feeling, not a claimed cultural performance peak.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep outward cues sparse and let one contextually meaningful care choice carry the depth.
levels.recovery: Return to the person’s actual preferences and the scene’s ordinary relational obligations.
levels.playable_direction: Let affection and sorrow be fully present while allowing this person to remain more than your concern.

cue_conflicts: All physical and acoustic cues here are editorial possibilities, not authenticated Ifaluk display rules.

emotions.context_notes: Culturally lexicalized label with explicitly limited editorial relational interpretation. Individual baseline, actual relationship, power, culture, language and mobility must come from the character and scene; this profile makes no claim of authentic Ifaluk facial, vocal, bodily, status or ritual performance.

emotions.label: Jealousy
emotions.definition: An unsettled response to a perceived rival threatening a valued bond, place, or exclusive significance; desire for reassurance can coexist with anger and self-doubt.
emotions.appraisal: Someone else may receive the attention or security that makes this relationship matter to me; the evidence may be ambiguous.
emotions.objective: Find out whether my place in the relationship is secure, while negotiating the impulse to monitor or claim it.
action_tendencies: Track exchanges involving the perceived rival
Seek reassurance or an explicit commitment
Interrupt, withdraw, or test the connection
Compare present attention with remembered closeness
distinctions: Envy concerns another person’s advantage; jealousy concerns a threatened bond or position.
Betrayal treats a violation as established; jealousy can arise before any violation.
Love does not require ownership, and jealousy does not establish love or justify control.

voice.texture: A dry edge or brittle brightness can reveal the effort to remain agreeable

voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A brief humorless laugh, swallowed reply, or audible exhale is optional

body.chest_torso: Torso orients to the bond even while the head pretends disinterest
body.arms_elbows: Elbows can close around personal space or open in a claiming gesture
body.hands_fingers: Fingers adjust an unnecessary object or stop midway toward contact
body.pelvis_weight: Weight shifts toward joining the exchange, then checks

body.gait: A route can bend to pass near the pair without rushing
body.proxemics: Distance becomes a question: approach for reassurance or retreat to protect pride

body.stillness: Stillness can be vigilant monitoring rather than relaxation

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: A passing exchange makes the character briefly question their importance, without yet accepting a threat.
levels.face: The eyes leave the current task for one extra look toward the pair. An inner brow gathers, then releases; the mouth keeps its ordinary shape except for a delayed answer-smile, and the chin turns back a beat late.
levels.voice: Keep the usual register and modest contours, with a thin bright edge on a casual question. Volume remains conversational; the next phrase comes fractionally early, followed by a short listening pause and an easy breath before resuming the original subject.
levels.body: The torso inclines toward the sound while the pelvis stays with the original task. A fingertip pauses on a prop; the nearest foot prepares a small turn, then settles as the character chooses to remain where they are.
levels.timing: Let the checking glance appear after a specific laugh, name, or shared reference rather than at random.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep the face socially available and place the entire concern in one delayed return to the task.
levels.recovery: Ordinary warmth can return as soon as inclusion is offered, with one residual glance toward the rival.
levels.playable_direction: Check whether that moment included you, then try to give the answer very little importance.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: A small comparison becomes personally relevant; the character wants confirmation without admitting why.
levels.face: The gaze follows the partner’s reaction more closely than the rival’s action. The lower lids gather, the brow holds a shallow crease, and a small social smile lingers after the cheeks have already relaxed, exposing its maintenance.
levels.voice: Stay near the normal register but lift the end of an apparently light question. A faintly dry tone sits beneath conversational volume; pace is tidier than usual, with a small breath before the rival’s name and a measuring pause after it.
levels.body: One shoulder rotates into the conversation, bringing the chest a little nearer while the feet keep an exit available. The hand finds a chair back or personal prop, briefly claiming an ordinary place without demanding attention.
levels.timing: Repeat the check once after new evidence; do not turn the sequence into continuous darting eyes.
levels.restrained_alternative: Ask the practical question cleanly, then reveal the concern only in how closely the answer is received.
levels.recovery: An unforced invitation restores breathing rhythm; the hand may release the object before the face fully softens.
levels.playable_direction: Find a harmless reason to rejoin the exchange and see whether your presence changes it.

levels.label: Clear

levels.face: The eyes move from the pair to the partner and remain there. Inner brows tighten, the lids narrow, and the lips flatten before a controlled half-smile returns; the jaw shifts once as an accusation is edited into a question.
levels.voice: Use a slightly lower register for the question’s central words, then a restrained upward turn inviting denial. Keep a clear, cool texture at moderate volume; speech slows around the evidence, with an audible ordinary inhale and a deliberate gap for an answer.
levels.body: The chest faces the partner squarely as the arms settle close to the ribs. Weight moves forward without crowding; the rear foot stays planted, and a hand that might touch instead rests against the character’s own wrist.
levels.timing: Allow the question to follow a failed attempt at casual inclusion, making the change of tactic visible.
levels.restrained_alternative: Keep brows smooth and words courteous; let unwavering attention carry the demand for reassurance.
levels.recovery: A convincing answer releases the jaw first, while orientation toward the partner remains for another exchange.
levels.playable_direction: Ask the question you can defend asking, while listening for the answer to the question underneath.

levels.label: Strong

levels.face: The brow contracts while the gaze holds the partner, then cuts once to the rival. The mouth opens on an immediate challenge and closes to reshape it; cheek tension and a raised chin make the effort at composure legible.
levels.voice: Drop into a firmer register with narrow, emphatic contours on relationship words. Choose a close, hard-edged conversational tone rather than automatic shouting; phrases arrive in short groups, interrupted by a restorative breath and a silence that asks the partner to choose.
levels.body: The torso advances half a step or its seated equivalent, then stops at an intentional boundary. Elbows flare briefly before returning inward; the hands open as if presenting evidence, while the feet resist the impulse to follow a departing partner.
levels.timing: Alternate one claiming beat with one self-check; avoid making pursuit the only available expression.
levels.restrained_alternative: Hold the body upright and keep the voice formally even, using one exact word to expose the stake.
levels.recovery: Reassurance must be specific now; release comes through questioning, lowered chin, and renewed willingness to share conversational space.
levels.playable_direction: Make your place unmistakable without assuming you have the right to control the other person.

levels.label: Intense
levels.felt_state: Attention repeatedly returns to possible exclusion, and reassurance is difficult to retain between new comparisons.
levels.face: The eyes search the partner’s face for contradiction, with fewer blinks during each answer. Brow tension spreads across the forehead; the lips compress, then part on an unfinished protest, and the jaw trembles or resets without requiring tears.
levels.voice: The register may alternate between a low demand and a higher, vulnerable question. Let the texture become strained or unusually polished at contained-to-firm volume; sentences accelerate toward the feared conclusion, then break for comfortable breaths and long, testing listening pauses.
levels.body: The ribcage remains aimed at the relationship even as the pelvis shifts toward withdrawal. Hands begin a contact request and retreat to the torso; knees or feet reset repeatedly, unable to settle on joining, confronting, or leaving the scene.
levels.timing: Each fresh cue can restart the sequence before the previous reassurance has fully registered.
levels.restrained_alternative: Make the whole encounter unnervingly polite, with precise posture and no spontaneous ease between spoken turns.
levels.recovery: Recovery needs a clear boundary or explicit reassurance; neutral conversation alone may leave the monitoring habit active.
levels.playable_direction: Try to obtain one assurance strong enough to survive the next thing you notice.

levels.label: Consuming
levels.felt_state: The perceived threat organizes almost every interpretation, displacing the character’s original purpose in the scene.
levels.face: The gaze fixes on one apparently decisive exchange and barely follows other speakers. The brow can become still with concentration; the lips hold an arrested reply, then thin, and the chin draws inward as exposure becomes as threatening as loss.
levels.voice: Use a close low register with a compressed contour, or a brittle high politeness if that suits the character. Volume can fall; a dry, carefully placed tone makes ordinary words laborious, with delayed starts, shortened phrases, and breaths taken between attempts to ask.
levels.body: Other tasks stop. The torso stays poised toward the partner while arms fold protectively or hang without purpose; weight is braced through the available support, and any movement becomes a single deliberate approach or withdrawal rather than restless general agitation.
levels.timing: Hold attention through interruptions, making it clear that other information is presently failing to compete.
levels.restrained_alternative: Deliver the practical conversation correctly while repeatedly missing easy social cues and invitations unrelated to the threat.
levels.recovery: A pause apart can loosen fixation; the character may need to name the fear before ordinary exchange becomes possible.
levels.playable_direction: Preserve the bond in your imagination while each new detail appears to argue against it.

levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: Fear of losing the bond overwhelms the ability to integrate reassurance; action may freeze instead of becoming louder.
levels.face: The face may go nearly blank while the eyes remain locked on the partner. A deep-set brow, rigid mouth corners, and a held chin replace expressive changes; a blink or failed smile arrives only after the partner directly addresses the character.
levels.voice: Allow a very low, small register with almost no contour, or one brief broken appeal followed by quiet. Texture is exposed and unsteady rather than forced; pace becomes sparse, with incomplete starts, ordinary recovery breaths, and long gaps where an answer cannot be organized.
levels.body: The body stops mid-transition between approach and retreat. The chest stays lifted against a drawn-back pelvis; arms lose their intended gesture, and feet or seated supports remain planted until a safe, chosen distance becomes possible without grabbing or blocking anyone.
levels.timing: Sustain the inability to choose for a specific beat, then let one manageable action replace total surveillance.
levels.restrained_alternative: Maintain immaculate social stillness; make the failure to process a simple reassurance the visible sign of overwhelming intensity.
levels.recovery: Reorientation begins with space, a concrete fact, and one completed breath or sentence; certainty need not return immediately.
levels.playable_direction: Let the wish to keep this person briefly exceed your ability to decide what to do next.

variants.label: Intimate-bond jealousy
variants.context: An adult partner fears losing relational significance to another person.
variants.objective: Ask for security while respecting the partner’s agency.
variants.face_modifier: Track the partner’s responsiveness more than the rival’s appearance.
variants.voice_modifier: Let familiar forms of address acquire unusual weight.
variants.body_modifier: Offer or withhold familiar consensual contact as a choice, never a claim of ownership.
variants.timing_modifier: Give shared rituals a delayed or interrupted rhythm.

variants.voice_modifier: Stress words identifying the shared team, history, or role.
variants.body_modifier: Orient to the group’s opening rather than placing the body between two people.
variants.timing_modifier: Let familiar turn-taking fail before the concern becomes explicit.

cue_conflicts: A claiming approach and a pride-protecting retreat are alternative tactics; choose one for each beat.
A polite smile can coexist with watchful eyes, but do not add a simultaneous broad joyful grin.

emotions.context_notes: Select cues against this character’s individual resting face, habitual voice, and regulation style. Relationship history and power change what can safely be shown; culture shapes gaze, touch, distance, and permission to speak. Translate weight shifts, movement, or prop actions to the character’s mobility and available shot framing. These are optional fictional performance choices, not evidence that a person necessarily feels this state.

emotions.label: Envy
emotions.definition: Painful or energizing comparison in which another person’s possession, quality, recognition, or opportunity highlights something the character wants and lacks.
emotions.appraisal: They have access to something that matters to me, and their advantage makes my own position feel insufficient.
emotions.objective: Manage the comparison by approaching the desired possibility, protecting self-worth, or reducing the other person’s apparent advantage.
action_tendencies: Seek a path toward similar opportunity
Devalue, conceal, or admit the wish
distinctions: Jealousy centers on threatened relational security; envy can involve no threatened bond.
Admiration values excellence without necessarily experiencing a painful personal deficit.
Envy may motivate constructive effort or hostile devaluation; neither follows inevitably.

face.brows_forehead: One brow may rise in assessment while the inner brow tightens
face.eyelids: Lids narrow over an appraising look, or remain open in reluctant interest
face.gaze: Gaze alternates between the advantage and a self-relevant comparison object
face.blink: Blinks punctuate looking away after comparison
face.cheeks: Cheeks may lift for congratulations while tension remains beside the mouth
face.nose_nostrils: A small nasal exhale can mark dismissal; no compulsory flare
face.lips_mouth: A congratulatory smile can become thin or close unevenly
face.jaw_chin: Chin lifts defensively or lowers toward private disappointment
face.head_neck: Head tilts to inspect, then withdraws to conceal investment
face.complexion: Color change is optional and nonspecific

voice.pitch_register: A public compliment may sit above the private baseline; admission may drop lower
voice.pitch_range_contour: Contours can brighten for praise then flatten on self-reference
voice.loudness: Maintain appropriate social volume or shrink it for an honest admission
voice.tempo_rhythm: Praise may come promptly while follow-up questions arrive with calculation
voice.stress: Stress the cost, access, luck, or distinguishing feature under comparison
voice.articulation: Careful consonants can make a compliment sound managed
voice.resonance: Social brightness may give way to a narrower, less open resonance
voice.texture: Choose polished cordiality, dryness, or exposed wistfulness according to tactic
voice.breath_phrasing: Take a comfortable breath between praising the other and mentioning yourself
voice.pauses: Pause before acknowledging the desired quality outright
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: A small congratulatory laugh or dismissive huff may be selected

body.head_neck: Head inclines toward the advantage despite a posture of indifference
body.shoulders: Shoulders square for comparison or sink briefly in private
body.chest_torso: Torso approaches to inspect, then closes when personal lack is felt
body.arms_elbows: Elbows stay neat in public or open with a request to examine
body.hands_fingers: Fingers compare a seam, award, screen, or personal item where appropriate
body.pelvis_weight: Weight approaches the opportunity before retreating into self-protection
body.legs_feet: Feet can remain directed at what the gaze pretends to leave
body.gait: Walking may circle toward a better view or deliberately pass without stopping
body.proxemics: The object of envy attracts attention without authorizing intrusion
body.touch_props: Touch remains permission-based; the character may handle their own lesser-valued object instead
body.stillness: Stillness can preserve dignity while comparison continues internally

levels.label: Trace
levels.felt_state: Another person’s advantage briefly catches the character’s attention and introduces an unwelcome self-comparison.
levels.face: The gaze rests on the desired feature, then checks the character’s own equivalent. A brow rises in appraisal; lips part for a compliment and close with a small delay, while the chin withdraws just enough to hide investment.
levels.voice: Keep normal register and rounded conversational contours, with a faint dryness on the comparison word. Volume stays easy; the compliment proceeds at ordinary pace, followed by a short pause and a quiet breath before attention returns to the shared topic.
levels.body: The torso inclines to inspect without leaving its original position. A hand briefly checks the character’s own prop or clothing; weight advances toward the advantage, then resets as the feet stay with the current social arrangement.
levels.timing: Place the comparison after a concrete reveal, such as a result, object, or account of an opportunity.
levels.restrained_alternative: Offer uncomplicated praise and let only a glance toward your own situation carry the private deficit.
levels.recovery: A broader view of the situation can dissolve the comparison before it affects the next exchange.
levels.playable_direction: Notice what you want before deciding whether admitting that want would cost you anything.

levels.label: Mild
levels.felt_state: The advantage matters enough that the character wants details, while still preserving a friendly surface.
levels.face: The eyes return to the feature despite an intended look away. Lower lids gather with assessment; the cheeks support a courteous smile while the mouth corners tighten, and the head tips as if asking a purely practical question.
levels.voice: Use a lightly elevated social register and an inquisitive contour, with polished rather than spontaneous warmth. Keep moderate volume and tidy pacing; emphasize access or effort, then pause after the answer, breathing easily while deciding whether it reduces the uncomfortable comparison.
levels.body: The chest remains open toward the other person, but the elbows draw closer during self-reference. Fingers settle on a personal possession; one foot edges toward the object or opportunity, stopping before a closer inspection would become an imposition.
levels.timing: Let each new detail either ease or sharpen the comparison rather than increasing tension on a fixed schedule.
levels.restrained_alternative: Ask one useful question in an even voice and keep the personal consequence private.
levels.recovery: Recognizing a reachable path can replace the thin smile with genuinely engaged curiosity and forward-oriented posture.
levels.playable_direction: Learn how they got it while trying not to reveal how much their answer matters.

levels.label: Clear
levels.felt_state: The character clearly experiences the other person’s good fortune as evidence of their own unmet wish.
levels.face: The gaze moves from the advantage to the other person’s face, searching for deservedness or access. Inner brows pinch; a smile appears for social duty, then drains from the cheeks before the lips release it, leaving the jaw briefly set.
levels.voice: Lower the register on a self-comparing aside, giving the contour a small downward turn. A dry or wistful tone sits at conversational volume; pace slows around “I” or “you,” with a breath before the admission and an unfinished pause afterward.
levels.body: Weight shifts away even as the head remains interested. The torso closes a little, a forearm crosses the waist, and the other hand starts an inspecting gesture before redirecting to a personal object; the feet preserve a socially acceptable distance.
levels.timing: Use a compliment followed by a self-reference to make the comparison explicit without requiring open hostility.
levels.restrained_alternative: Let a perfectly formed congratulation arrive a beat late; keep the body formal while the gaze retains the wish.
levels.recovery: An honest naming of the desire can reduce covert comparison even when the material difference remains.
levels.playable_direction: Tell them one true good thing, then confront what saying it reveals about your own wish.

levels.label: Strong
levels.felt_state: Comparison begins organizing the conversation; the character needs a way to restore a threatened sense of adequacy.
levels.face: The eyes inspect flaws or qualifying details, with a lifted outer brow and tightened lower lids. The mouth forms a precise smile that does not spread through the cheeks; the chin rises as the character prepares a balancing fact.
levels.voice: Use a firmer mid-to-low register, narrow contour, and a cool evaluative tone. Volume need not rise; sentences become pointed and neatly paced, emphasizing luck, cost, or limitation, then leaving a small silence and ordinary breath for the balancing claim to land.
levels.body: The torso straightens as if entering a comparison the character had not chosen. Elbows separate for a factual gesture, hands indicate a relevant detail, and weight settles back on the support while the feet stop approaching the desired thing.
levels.timing: Place the defensive qualification after enough acknowledgment that its purpose can be recognized.
levels.restrained_alternative: Maintain courteous brightness while selectively asking only questions that might diminish the other person’s advantage.
levels.recovery: A useful next step toward the character’s own goal can replace defensive comparison with purposeful movement.
levels.playable_direction: Find a way to stand level with them without pretending the thing they have does not matter.

levels.label: Intense
levels.felt_state: The desired advantage becomes difficult to separate from self-worth, making praise, proximity, and disclosure increasingly costly.
levels.face: The gaze catches repeatedly on the advantage, then breaks away sharply. Brow tension remains during attempted smiles; lips press against an unspoken complaint, and the jaw shifts as the character decides between admiration, admission, and cutting dismissal.
levels.voice: Let register rise briefly on an overbright compliment, then fall into a dry, exposed admission or pointed aside. Keep volume controlled-to-firm; pace bunches around comparisons, with abrupt stops, a comfortable settling breath, and longer pauses when the other person offers generosity.
levels.body: The chest pulls back while the head continues to seek information. Fingers stop their idle work and hold a prop too deliberately; knees or feet reposition for departure, but the torso turns back when another detail about the advantage becomes available.
levels.timing: Build a loop of involuntary interest and self-protective withdrawal, each triggered by new information.
levels.restrained_alternative: Remain technically gracious, allowing only reduced spontaneity and an unwillingness to linger after congratulations.
levels.recovery: Leaving the comparison frame or accepting a concrete invitation can gradually restore broader attention and ordinary vocal warmth.
levels.playable_direction: Stay close enough to understand the opportunity while protecting yourself from what each detail seems to say about you.

levels.label: Consuming
levels.felt_state: Comparison dominates the character’s sense of the scene, and even unrelated information is translated into unequal worth.
levels.face: The eyes become fixed on one symbol of the advantage. Forehead movement can diminish into sustained concentration; the mouth holds a small unspeaking line, cheek responsiveness falls away, and the chin retracts when another person invites genuine celebration.
levels.voice: Use a low, flattened register with a carefully smooth or depleted texture. Volume may become small; responses arrive late and economical, with little contour, a breath before each new social obligation, and a silence where a generous spontaneous reaction would normally occur.
levels.body: The body remains present but stops participating in celebration. Arms settle close to the trunk, a prop stays unused, and weight becomes heavy in the chair or planted feet; movement resumes only to inspect the advantage or preserve an exit.
levels.timing: Let missed social entries reveal that comparison is absorbing attention otherwise available to the room.
levels.restrained_alternative: Perform every expected social action accurately while leaving no room for spontaneous elaboration or relaxed contact.
levels.recovery: Recovery may begin by separating the desired resource from personal worth; behavior can soften before the wish itself changes.
levels.playable_direction: Let everything in the room briefly become evidence in a comparison you are tired of making.

levels.label: Overwhelming
levels.felt_state: The comparison overwhelms the ability to hold a stable sense of personal worth or participate honestly in the shared moment.
levels.face: The gaze may drop from the advantage and refuse another look. Inner brows hold together above quiet eyes; the mouth opens without a social reply, then closes, while a lowered chin and motionless cheeks replace earlier efforts at congratulations.
levels.voice: Allow a nearly level, low register and exposed, sparse tone, or one brief admission in a higher register before quiet. Keep sound comfortable and potentially soft; words separate by long pauses and ordinary breaths as the character abandons the performance of easy celebration.
levels.body: The torso folds inward or becomes rigidly upright, choosing one protective form. Hands release the comparison object and settle against the body; weight grounds through chair or feet, and the character seeks space without taking, damaging, or obstructing another person’s possession.
levels.timing: Use the failure of one expected gracious response as the apex, followed by a deliberate boundary or exit.
levels.restrained_alternative: Offer a short correct congratulation, then become very still because continuing the social performance is no longer manageable.
levels.recovery: Space, self-directed purpose, or a humane acknowledgment of the wish can restart contact without erasing the unequal circumstance.
levels.playable_direction: Stop trying to win the comparison long enough to admit how much the unmet wish hurts.

variants.label: Aspirational envy
variants.context: The other person’s advantage is painful but also suggests an attainable direction.
variants.objective: Convert the comparison into a path the character can choose.
variants.face_modifier: Let inspection return to the useful feature rather than only the other person’s status.
variants.voice_modifier: Questions can gain genuine warmth as practical information becomes available.
variants.body_modifier: Gradually orient toward an actionable tool, task, or next step.
variants.timing_modifier: Allow discovery to interrupt the comparison loop.

seven_levels.modifier: Catch the small pang, then inspect what specifically attracts you instead of judging your whole position.
Ask one question about process, discovering whether the advantage contains a skill or opportunity you can pursue.
Admit that you want something similar, letting the honesty reduce the effort of polite concealment.
Request a concrete route forward while keeping your disappointment about the present difference visible.
Accept useful guidance without pretending the comparison has stopped hurting; let the next action become more important than appearances.
Interrupt repeated self-comparison with one chosen task, allowing attention to narrow around a workable first step.
Name the desire and defer judgment about your worth; choose a small action only after enough space returns.

variants.label: Resentful comparison
variants.context: The advantage feels undeserved, unfairly distributed, or inaccessible.
variants.objective: Protect self-respect while deciding whether and how to challenge the apparent inequality.
variants.face_modifier: Search for evidence about fairness; avoid treating an unattractive face as proof of envy.
variants.voice_modifier: Stress access, rules, or unequal treatment rather than automatically insulting the other person.
variants.body_modifier: Place the body in relation to the gate or process that distributes the advantage.
variants.timing_modifier: Let evidence of unfairness sharpen the beat more than the object’s beauty.

seven_levels.modifier: Notice who received the opportunity and check whether the same rule applied to everyone else.
Ask about the selection process, keeping the first challenge small enough to receive an informative answer.
Identify the specific unequal condition before turning disappointment into a general accusation against the recipient.
Put a balancing fact into the conversation, then watch whether it is acknowledged or politely ignored.
Choose between questioning the system and diminishing the person; make the choice visible in whom you address.
Withdraw from ceremonial praise when participation feels like endorsing an unfair allocation you cannot presently change.
State the unfairness or take space, allowing intense personal pain without turning retaliation into an inevitable outcome.

temporal_arc.onset: A valued advantage becomes visible and triggers a personally relevant comparison.
temporal_arc.escalation: Attention shifts from the feature itself toward what the disparity appears to imply about the self.
temporal_arc.apex: The character admits the wish, devalues the advantage, pursues a path, or cannot continue the comparison.
temporal_arc.recovery: New perspective, agency, distance, or an honest conversation makes other measures of worth available.
temporal_arc.carryover: The desired quality may remain attractive after the painful comparison subsides.

transitions.trigger: The character can value the other’s achievement without treating it as a verdict on self.
transitions.bridge: Release the balancing qualification and allow a direct, specific acknowledgment.

transitions.trigger: A reachable next step appears.
transitions.bridge: Move the gaze from the other person’s advantage to the character’s own available work.

transitions.trigger: The unequal outcome is interpreted as repeated, unfair treatment.
transitions.bridge: Let comparison settle into remembered grievance and a more durable boundary.

prompt_example.spoken_text: I thought you would be here.
prompt_example.visual_direction: Notice the symbol of their success, glance at your own unused place, then meet their eyes with a carefully completed smile.
prompt_example.delivery_direction: Sound sincerely glad on the first words, then let “you” carry the private comparison before a small, controlled pause.

cue_conflicts: Aspirational approach and defensive devaluation are different tactics; do not play both at full strength in the same beat.
Warm congratulations may be sincere alongside envy; avoid making every smile deceitful.
High envy can reduce speech and movement instead of escalating to insults or sabotage.
emotions.context_notes: Select cues against this character’s individual resting face, habitual voice, and regulation style. Relationship history and power change what can safely be shown; culture shapes gaze, touch, distance, and permission to speak. Translate weight shifts, movement, or prop actions to the character’s mobility and available shot framing. These are optional fictional performance choices, not evidence that a person necessarily feels this state.

emotions.label: Trust
emotions.definition: A willingness to accept meaningful vulnerability because the character expects another person, relationship, or process to respond reliably enough.
emotions.appraisal: I cannot control every outcome, but this person or arrangement has earned enough confidence for me to rely on it.
emotions.objective: Hand over a meaningful share of control, information, or responsibility while retaining the ability to choose boundaries.
action_tendencies: Rely on a promise or skill
Allow another person to act without constant checking
distinctions: Calm describes a settled state; trust can coexist with danger and intense arousal.
Love describes attachment; trust requires confidence about a relevant vulnerability and may be absent in a loved relationship.
Trust is not automatic compliance, lack of boundaries, or certainty that nothing can go wrong.

voice.pitch_range_contour: Contours complete without turning every statement into a checking question
voice.loudness: Volume suits distance and circumstance rather than proving confidence
voice.tempo_rhythm: Phrases can finish at an unhurried pace; urgent trust can remain fast
voice.stress: Stress the shared task, permission, or specific entrusted responsibility
voice.articulation: Words can be plain and clear without legalistic overprecision
voice.resonance: Resonance may become less guarded and more conversationally open
voice.texture: Choose candid warmth, professional steadiness, or exposed honesty
voice.breath_phrasing: Let comfortable breaths occur without hiding every vulnerable pause
voice.pauses: Silences make room for the other person rather than testing them
voice.nonverbal_vocalizations: An accepting hum, relieved exhale, or quiet acknowledgment may be useful
